Infantino had succeeded in keeping Fifa’s plans under wraps until reports of the proposal first emerged in the Times and Financial Times. Fifa council members are understood to have been surprised by the announcement, having been sidelined from the decision‑making process.

It is the second occasion that Infantino has attempted to attract private capital to fund Fifa. In 2018, he agreed a deal in principle with the Japanese bank SoftBank to provide $25bn in funding for an expanded Club World Cup and global Nations League, but failed to get sufficient support, largely due to opposition from Europe. Uefa and the clubs are again united against Fifa’s plans, but Infantino may have enough backing from elsewhere to be able to disregard them.

In its statement, Fifa said the new enterprise would enable it to increase the funding provided to each of the associations from $8m to $20m each year, a huge sum for the majority of their 211 members.

Fifa insisted it would retain responsibility for football’s governance and the international match calendar, but in reality inviting private investment in its commercial rights would subject the decision makers to significant external pressures. Investors could ultimately be given significant influence over decisions that affect the entire sport, leading to fears they would seek to stage the World Cup more regularly and permit it to be hosted in only the most lucrative markets, such as the US. Fifa said it would “carefully select long-term investors who will purchase minority, non-controlling interests in FFE – all net benefits of FFE will be reinvested back into football worldwide”.

Infantino is expected to be re‑elected unopposed as president next year despite the huge controversy he attracts, but under Fifa statutes must stand down in 2031 after serving three full terms. The Times reported, however, that Infantino has aspirations to serve as chair of the new commercial company, which could earn him tens of millions of dollars.

Sports.title: Abusive chanting against immigrants in English football on rise, new data reveals
Sports.content:
Abusive chanting against immigrants has become a feature of football matches in England, according to new data from Kick It Out.

Last season 39 reports of anti-immigrant chanting were made to the anti-discrimination charity, more than the previous two seasons combined. Phrases such as “stop the boats” and “send them back” were reported as being heard “at all levels of the game”, as part of a growing trend of discriminatory “mass chanting” at matches, Kick It Out said.

The growth in anti-immigrant rhetoric was consistent with a broader rise in reports of discrimination, at matches and online. Kick It Out received 1,744 reports of discriminatory behaviour in total during the 2025-26 season, a record and a 25% increase on the previous campaign.

The number of reported incidents increased across every type of discrimination to new highs. Reports of racism remained the most common, rising 19% year-on-year, the 792 reports making up 45% of the total. Complaints of sexist behaviour rose 12% to 216, homophobia rose 46% to 203, antisemitism rose 43% to 93, ableism rose 20% to 89, and Islamophobia rose 88% to 60. Kick it Out said all six areas had seen their biggest totals in five years.

Reports of abuse in grassroots football rose for a fifth consecutive year, up by 33% in 2025-26 to a record 248 reports. Equally, the 98 reports of abuse against match officials was the same as the past three seasons combined.

Samuel Okafor, chief executive at Kick It Out, said such behaviour at matches and in online spaces was matched by a rise in hateful rhetoric elsewhere in British society, but he praised the willingness of supporters – and players – to speak out.

“These figures show that discrimination remains deeply embedded across the game at a time when we’re also seeing rises in hate crime and divisive political rhetoric in Britain,” he said. “But they also show that people are more willing to stand up to abuse when they see it, and it’s encouraging to see professional players set that example last season.”

For example, in March, a 60-year-old man was given a suspended sentence for sending offensive messages to the England Women defender Jess Carter, who went public over the attacks during the European Championship last year. In the men’s game, Antoine Semenyo drew attention to the racist abuse he had received over the course of the season, with a charge of racially aggravated behaviour against one man scheduled to go to trial in September.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Kick It Out’s findings concur with those reported by the UK Football Policing Unit last week. The police said that some of the increase could be explained by improved reporting mechanisms, with misogynist abuse only introduced as a separate category of discrimination at the start of last season. Both police and Kick It Out have called on online platforms to do more to stop abuse.

Okafor said: “We will continue to work with football authorities, clubs, leagues, regulators and government to ensure we match the courage shown to report abuse with clear and consistent action so that football is welcoming to everyone.”

Sports.title: Retaining Rodri is key to Manchester City success under Enzo Maresca
Sports.content:
“Welcome home,” was Khaldoon al-Mubarak’s warm greeting to Enzo Maresca on his appointment last month as Manchester City manager. Now, after two previous spells at the club, the Italian’s task is to keep the chair content, and ensure a three-year contract does not end early. To achieve that, Maresca’s tenure must continue Pep Guardiola’s glittering legacy of 20 trophies across a decade of excellence.

The key to the 46-year-old, who was Guardiola’s assistant during the 2022-23 treble season and City’s elite development squad leader two years before that, being successful can be summed up in two words: “Keep Rodri”. Yet with Real Madrid almost certain to launch a bid for the peerless No 6, and him seemingly wanting to play for the Spanish giants, a move away from City may become inevitable.

Maresca’s best hope of avoiding “doing a David Moyes” – who succeeded Sir Alex Ferguson at Manchester United in May 2013 and lasted a mere 34 Premier League games – and thriving as the man who follows the man is to retain Rodri, who has just captained Spain to World Cup glory, winning the Golden Ball as best player in the process. The 30-year-old is contracted until June. City’s stance is that they have no wish to sell and remain intent on persuading him to sign the new terms that have been on offer for a while.

Saying City will definitely be contenders for the biggest prizes next season if they retain Rodri may sound simplistic until you examine his CV and are reminded of the pivotal role he has played for the club. Rodri was key to City’s treble glory, including scoring the winner in the Champions League final against Inter. Then there was the 74-game unbeaten sequence with him in the colours that ran from February 2023 to May 2024. “He’s unbelievable, irreplaceable,” said Guardiola. “The best midfielder in the world by far.”

The World Cup triumph also came after Rodri had been part of Spain’s Euro 2024 glory and City’s 2023 Club World Cup success, again winning the player of the tournament in each. In the two seasons before the World Cup, injury plagued him, however. The result: no Premier League titles in either year for City, halting a record four-in-a-row run for Guardiola’s garlanded team.

Rodri’s ability to mould and control contests was reiterated by his World Cup displays. Exhibit A: the chokehold imposed on France in the semi-finals. At domestic and international level, this is a priceless quality. So if Maresca can field Rodri, City will be feared in the league and on the continent. The back injury for which Rodri underwent surgery on Monday is minor, but the desire to broaden his club horizons – primarily in Spain – remains, meaning there is no certainty he will stay put. Particularly so given the initial resistance of Real Madrid’s president, Florentino Pérez, to acquiring Rodri has shifted, due, surely, to his resurgence at the World Cup and maybe José Mourinho, returning as head coach, expressing a need for the player’s calm and elan.

View image in fullscreen Enzo Maresca worked under Pep Guardiola as Manchester City won the treble in 2023. Photograph: Adam Vaughan/EPA

City have invested £116m on Elliot Anderson this summer, an England first-choice midfielder who may be joined by another midfielder in Lille’s Ayyoub Bouaddi, the 18-year-old who also impressed at the World Cup for Morocco, and would cost around £85m. However, neither of them or Tijjani Reijnders, Mateo Kovacic nor Nico González can claim to be in the class of Rodri, who may well be in line to claim a second Ballon d’Or following his World Cup exploits.

Maresca won the Championship with Leicester in 2024 and the following season led Chelsea to fourth in the Premier League and to a Conference League triumph, following that up with glory at the expanded Club World Cup, which featured the 3-0 demolition of Paris Saint-Germain in the final. All of this convinced al-Mubarak and his chief executive, Ferran Soriano, that Maresca is the one who can thrive after the era-defining Guardiola.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Quick Guide Gvardiol says 'great things' will happen under Maresca Show Joško Gvardiol has signed a new five-year contract with Manchester City, the defender stating that “great things” can be achieved with Enzo Maresca, the new manager. While the terms include an option of a further 12-months, the Croatian is confident that the Italian’s first season will be successful. “I remember when he was at Chelsea [2024-26] it was difficult to play against them – especially away. We struggled. He’s here and I think we can achieve some great things together,” Gvardiol said. The 24-year-old has made 122 appearances and claimed six trophies with City since joining from RB Leipzig in 2023 for £77m and was voted the club’s 2024-5 player of the season. Gvardiol said: “I remember my first season when I arrived – back then I was kind of still young. In these three years I’ve learned a lot of things from all my team-mates, my friends in the dressing room and on the pitch in the last three years. "I still think there are a lot of things to improve and learn but I’m only 24, I have enough time.” Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

However, as Maresca made clear with his “after Sir Alex [Ferguson]” reference in his unveiling on Friday, directly following greatness can be treacherous. The comparison between him and Moyes is hardly precise, though. Moyes arrived at United trophyless and with no experience of the pressures of an elite club. Maresca’s résumé shows a season and a half in the Chelsea hothouse and, with his prior experience of City, he is versed in the organisation where he now plays a crucial role.

City have five weeks of the market remaining to try to persuade Rodri his future is at the club. Guardiola’s stance was never to stop any player exiting who wished to do so. The logic is understandable: what is the point in retaining an unhappy employee? In this case it would also be one who wants to return to his native city. “Having played for Atlético [Madrid] before would not prevent me from playing for Real Madrid,” Rodri said in March. “There are other players who have done that before. Maybe not direct transfers, but eventually. You can’t turn down one of the world’s best clubs.”

Even Real Madrid boycotting Rodri’s Ballon d’Or-crowning ceremony in November 2024 in protest at Vinícius Júnior’s failure to win the vote has clearly not dissuaded the midfielder that the Bernabéu can be the home al-Mubarak characterises City as for Maresca.

Sports.title: Xabi Alonso plays down Welbeck and Henderson moves after Chelsea win
Sports.content:
Xabi Alonso refused to confirm Chelsea are interested in signing the veterans Danny Welbeck and Jordan Henderson after his first game in charge of the team, a 6-4 pre-season victory against Western Sydney Wanderers on Tuesday, but said he was looking to build a squad that had “proper balance”.

Chelsea are understood to be in talks over a surprise move to sign the 35-year-old Welbeck from Brighton, with the club also reportedly interested in signing the 36-year-old Henderson from Brentford. The links to two Premier League stalwarts reflects a revised transfer strategy under Alonso, with Chelsea seeking to recruit more experienced players into their squad as opposed to focused solely on signing young players, often tying them to lengthy contracts.

“I’m sure that from today to the last day of the transfer [window] there will be a lot of links, a lot of rumours, so to be commenting on all of them, it’s going to be a hard task,” Alonso said. “But for sure, we need proper balance in terms of qualities, in terms of positions, in terms of balance. We want to have a complete squad and we want to make a good team.”

The new Chelsea manager fielded a youthful side at the Accor Stadium at Sydney Olympic Park in Homebush, with Liam Delap and Tosin Adarabioyo the most experienced members of the starting lineup. Alonso waited until the 63rd minute to bring on a host of star names, including Cole Palmer and João Pedro. The Brazilian forward, who missed out on a place in Carlo Ancelotti’s World Cup squad, made a significant impact off the bench, scoring a hat-trick in just nine minutes as Chelsea took control of the game against their A-League opponents.

João Pedro scored 20 goals during an excellent debut season for Chelsea, having arrived from Brighton for £60m 12 months ago, and asked about the player’s mood before the upcoming campaign, Alonso said: “Very hungry. João is really, really determined to have a great season. He wants to, after a great last year, when he scored many goals. He wants to keep scoring more and more.”

A number of Chelsea’s youngsters showed plenty of promise, with the 17-year-old Dastan Satpayev opening the scoring after six minutes. The Kazakh forward is yet to sign officially for the club and is playing in pre-season as a triallist. His opening goal came from a defence-splitting pass from another teenager, Ryan Kavuma-McQueen, with Satpayev smashing the ball home at the near post.

Chelsea’s back four struggled in the first half against a lively Wanderers frontline and their reported new set-piece coach, Aston Villa’s Austin MacPhee, will have plenty to work on judging by the ease with which Brandon Borrello and Anthony Pantazopoulos won headers from a corner as the latter scored at the back post for the hosts.

View image in fullscreen João Pedro scored a nine-minute hat-trick after coming on as a second-half substitute. Photograph: Mark Evans/EPA

The Wanderers took the lead through Aydan Hammond before a lovely finish from the Portuguese midfielder Dário Essugo made it 2-2 at the break. The goals kept coming in the second half when the left-back Landon Emenalo, who impressed going forward, saw his clearance deflected into the path of Dylan Scicluna, who put the Sydney side 3-2 ahead. Alonso then turned to his bench and his substitutions made an immediate impact. João Pedro held off a number of challenges on the edge of the box before pulling the ball back to Jamie Gittens, who fired home from close range.

But this topsy-turvy game, which felt like England’s third-place playoff against France at the World Cup and finished with the same scoreline, provided more entertainment as the Australian side went ahead for a third time after Estêvão Willian lost possession on the edge of his own area. Awan Lual was on hand to slide the ball through Robert Sánchez’s legs to put his side 4-3 ahead.

The Wanderers, who are also in pre-season, again failed to hold on to a lead as Chelsea overpowered a team that finished bottom of their domestic league last season. João Pedro looked sharp as he showed great composure to score twice in five minutes, before scrambling home an effort from a corner to wrap up his match-winning exploits.

João Pedro’s performance was in stark contrast to that of Delap, who has been repeatedly linked with a move away from west London. The 23-year-old endured another frustrating evening for Chelsea, going close on two occasions but failing to find the back of the net. Assessing Delap’s attitude since returning from the summer break, Alonso said: “I see him in a good mood, in a good desire to get proper fitness, proper football, feeling good and he’s doing great.”

Sports.title: Milos Kerkez: ‘I’m delighted – Andoni Iraola is the perfect fit for Liverpool’
Sports.content:
It has been quite the summer for Milos Kerkez. There was time at home in Serbia, holidays in Montenegro and Spain, a frantic knock on his bedroom door one day to tell him that Arne Slot had been sacked, an unexpected reunion with Andoni Iraola shortly afterwards, and thousands of well‑wishes sent his way after being photographed escorting a bride into church in his hometown of Vrbas. Congratulations on the wedding are also extended at the start of our interview on a rooftop terrace at Liverpool’s team hotel.

“No! This is wrong, everyone gets this wrong!” the full-back exclaims. “It was my oldest brother. In Serbia it is normal for the younger brothers to take the bride to the church. That’s what I did and now everyone thinks I got married. It was Rade, not me. There are three of us – Rade is the oldest, I’m the youngest and Marko is the middle one. I keep having to explain to people that I never got married. I was going around the club when we started back and people were congratulating me. I’m like: ‘No, I’m not ready for this yet!’”

Well, that’s one way of breaking the ice with an interviewee. Marriage is categorically not on the agenda for Kerkez, a humorous and engaging force of energy, but he is ready to embrace other responsibilities: notably stepping out of Andy Robertson’s shadow and stepping up at Liverpool. Early days, of course, but it has been noted during Liverpool’s pre‑season training camp at Chicago Fire’s performance centre how the 22-year-old and his fellow Hungary international Dominik Szoboszlai have taken a leading role among a relatively young squad.

Kerkez – who was eligible to play for Hungary through his paternal grandparents – is in an advantageous position as the Iraola era begins with gruelling double training sessions and a pre-season friendly win over Sunderland in Nashville on Saturday. He knows the new boss better than any other Liverpool player, having matured into a £40m left-back during two seasons with Iraola at Bournemouth. He knows he doesn’t have to win over the new head coach as Iraola rates him highly. And he knows that, to convince Liverpool fans after a difficult debut season at Anfield, he is now working for a coach who can bring the best out of him.

View image in fullscreen Milos Kerkez tussles with Newcastle’s Anthony Elanga during a difficult debut season at Anfield. Photograph: Adam Vaughan/EPA

“I was delighted, honestly,” Kerkez says on discovering Liverpool’s choice to replace Slot. “He helped me and improved me a lot in the two years I spent with him. I was really happy, obviously for myself but also for the team. Everyone knows what type of football he plays so I think he is the perfect fit for us.

“It’s the intensity. He’s not scared to play one-on-one all over the pitch, to press high and to be on the front foot always. If you see footage of how we all are after training, all lying down, then you can see what he is preparing us for. You definitely need legs and good condition for what he wants us to do, but we will be all right. When we play games with three or four teams he calls it ‘consequences’ and the losing team and the team that finishes second has to run. How much you have to run depends on what he decides in that moment, but there is always running for the team that loses.

“He’s intense and he likes details. He’s very professional. He likes to talk sometimes but not a lot. I think maybe he doesn’t want to get too close to some players and wants to show that everyone is the same in the team, so he doesn’t want to get too close to anyone in particular. He keeps it professional, with a lot of hard work.”

There were times last season when Kerkez appeared inhibited by Slot’s insistence on building from the back and full-backs coming inside. It was his pace and energy up and down the flank with Bournemouth that had attracted Liverpool and earned him a place in the Professional Footballers’ Association’s team of the year in 2024-25. He should be able to play to his strengths more often next season.

As he explains: “The gaffer likes to play more with the full-backs down the line, underlapping, overlapping. It worked well for me at Bournemouth, so I think it will also work well for me here. He always told me that defending is really important, for him that is first of all, and because you are a full-back you need to defend really hard. Everything you can do in front of you is like a bonus. So I was always focused first on defending and then running forward to help the wingers. He showed me that when you do your job then you are free to do what you want, so I felt really free with him. He lets you be more free to do your stuff.”

Not that Kerkez blames Slot for last season’s turbulence, far from it. The pair remain in contact. “I was surprised,” he says of the Dutchman’s sacking, 12 months after delivering the Premier League title. “I really didn’t know. I was back in Serbia, I was sleeping and my brother woke me up. He knocks on my door and it was a big surprise. Nobody knew. I couldn’t believe it, I was like: ‘Wow.’ I have been in touch with him since, we have exchanged a few messages.”

View image in fullscreen Milos Kerkez celebrates scoring at a time he was playing brilliantly well for Andoni Iraola at Bournemouth. Photograph: Scott Heppell/Reuters

Kerkez admits last season was “tough for everyone” at Liverpool as every time the team seemed to have solved one problem, another would appear. As part of the expensive recruitment drive of last summer that failed to bear fruit – though Kerkez achieved far more than others – the scrutiny on the left-back and his fellow new signings was particularly intense. He insists he did not feel it.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“Honestly, I don’t care about pressure,” says the full-back, who will face Wrexham in the second game of Liverpool’s US tour in New York on Wednesday. “I don’t like ‘pressure’ and that stuff. I grew up a bit different in Serbia. We grew up different. You could say maybe we are built a bit different. For example, I started to drive a truck when I was 10 years old.” Sorry? “It was with my dad,” Kerkez says. “I climbed in and then I took the wheel. He was doing the pedals, I was only quite small so I couldn’t reach them.”

Kerkez’s father, Sebastijan, still drives his son to Liverpool’s training centre on occasions. He and Kerkez’s mother, Tijana, moved to England to help their second son settle into life as a Premier League player. “They are very important,” says the defender. “My brothers have their own lives now but my parents are with me and I am much happier they are with me. My dad is here to smack me sometimes on the top of the head and to remind me. Sometimes you play a few good games and maybe you start to get a bit carried away. But my dad is here to smack me. I come straight back down and I switch straight back on.”

Another important influence on Kerkez has been Robertson, the man – and the Liverpool legend – he was bought to replace. The Scotland captain and now Tottenham left-back regularly took Kerkez aside last season to pass on his experience. But there was no big parting message when the time came for Robertson to say goodbye to Anfield in May.

“I didn’t want to get a lot on to him,” says Kerkez, who became close friends with Mohamed Salah last season. “He was a bit emotional as everything was coming to an end. I didn’t want to get on to him too much, but throughout the year he helped me. We had a few conversations about crosses and about the big lungs we need to have so we can run until tomorrow. He did a lot of seasons, I should also have the same. We had conversations like that. Also, where to put the last ball, to focus, to put your head up and sometimes put better crosses in.

“We all know what Andy did for the club. I’m not running away from that. I want to make my own way. I’m going to work hard. I know what it means to play for Liverpool. I showed it a bit last year and I am going to show it more this year. Before we left the Axa [Liverpool’s training ground, to come to Chicago] I saw on TV a show about how many goals and assists Mo had, it was something like 380. I just walked out! ‘What is this?’ I was thinking. Time flies. A new generation comes and hopefully everything will be good.”

Sports.title: Wrexham face Liverpool with Premier League still in their sights despite setback
Sports.content:
The Wrexham co-owner Ryan Reynolds called it a “punch-me moment” – his club playing Liverpool in a pre-season friendly at Yankee Stadium just five years after he and Rob McElhenney (now simply Rob Mac) completed their takeover of a club languishing in the National League. The knockout blow would be playing Liverpool at Anfield in the Premier League in 2027-28 and the manager, Phil Parkinson, accepts there is expectation on Wrexham to complete their remarkable rise through the divisions next season.

Parkinson’s team face Liverpool with confidence in the Bronx on Wednesday having defeated Manchester United and Leeds in pre-season so far and moved on from the anguish of missing out on the Championship playoffs on the final day of last season. The near-miss was undoubtedly a setback to an ambitious club’s grand vision but finishing seventh in the Championship at the first time of asking, Parkinson insists, was an accomplishment that should not be dismissed lightly.

The Wrexham manager said: “If we’re honest, to say five years down the line we’d have finished seventh in the Championship we would have said that was going to take some going. To get three promotions back-to-back-to-back is unheralded. Even though there’s always been ambition within the club and we’ve had resources, to take the club from the National League to seventh in the Championship is a lot of big steps and particularly the one last year. League One to the Championship is a huge step.

“Of course we would have loved to have got in the playoffs but I think the staff and the players should be really very proud of their achievements because that was a tough ask, especially with making so many changes.”

Wrexham are among the favourites for promotion next season but are the only Championship club not to make a signing – though a deal for Crystal Palace full-back Danny Imray is close – and will not be the only well-funded team with that aim, given the parachute payments available to relegated West Ham, Burnley and Wolves.

“I think the division is going to be stronger this season with the teams coming down,” Parkinson says. “We’ve got work to do within the squad to make us competitive again. We’re close to one signing but we need several more before the window closes. We have to be patient and we will be, but the squad’s not where we want it to be, to be competitive to meet the demands of a Championship season.

“It is going to be a tough second season, we know that, but we feel there is more to come from the existing group. It was difficult last season with a lot of players coming in later and having to relocate to the area and settle as the season started, but they were great for us and I feel there is more to come this season.”

Sports.title: ‘He’s back’: Zinedine Zidane named France head coach in long-awaited homecoming
Sports.content:
For Tuesday’s front page, L’Équipe simply went with “Il revient” – “He’s back” – echoing the newspaper’s 2005 headline when Zinedine Zidane came out of international retirement. At the time, the midfielder’s upcoming return was seen as a major boost to Les Bleus’ ailing World Cup qualifying campaign. There was a similar sense of anticipation now as the roads around the French Football Federation headquarters in Paris were closed off for Zidane’s unveiling as head coach. A crowd of France fans had gathered outside by the overground Métro tracks with flags, flares and drums, as more than a hundred journalists and TV cameras were ushered into the building.

The fact that Zidane would be next in line to lead France after Didier Deschamps had been an open secret for several years and by the end of the World Cup his arrival was all but confirmed. The new head coach entered the press conference room on Tuesday morning only minutes after his appointment was confirmed by the FFF’s executive committee, but the feeling in France was that the occasion was a couple of decades in the making.

“It’s a new cycle,” the FFF president, Philippe Diallo, said after a preamble in which he paid tribute to Deschamps’ 14-year tenure. Talks with the 1998 World Cup hero, Diallo said, began in February 2025, the month after Deschamps announced he would step down this summer. “Zinedine Zidane is one of the legends of French football and he had made it known that it was one of his dreams to manage the French national team,” Diallo said. “We wanted someone with the aura, the ability, and the hearts of our fans and the French people to manage what is one of the best national teams in the world.”

View image in fullscreen France supporters gather in Paris to celebrate the confirmation of one of the greatest players in Les Bleus’ history as their new head coach. Photograph: Teresa Suárez/EPA

For Zidane, this announcement was the culmination of nearly half a decade of waiting in the wings. “I had several offers from clubs in the last four to five years, but I turned them all down for France,” the former Real Madrid manager said. “The national team is the only thing I wanted. I’ve been with the French teams since I was a kid, all the way up to the senior team. I’m a bit emotional. You might not be able to tell, but I am incredibly excited.”

Zidane declared it was the greatest day of his managerial career. “It’s an immense joy. I am ready for the challenge.”

The five years that have passed since the end of Zidane’s second spell in Madrid will have been spent preparing to take over Les Bleus. “I’ve been watching France as a supporter, but also as a future manager. I don’t think there are any traps. It’s new to me, but I’m not scared. This is what I wanted.” The 54-year-old’s first public appearance as head coach was light on the details of his plans for the national team. He notably sidestepped a question about whether Kylian Mbappé would retain the armband, insisting that he would have to meet the team and its “extraordinary players” first of all. “We need to keep this team winning,” he said, adding that he was impressed with what he had seen during the World Cup.

“I was a No 10 in my playing days,” he said when asked about the style of play he would look to implement. Whether his answer implies a continuation of Deschamps’ attacking shift remains to be seen, but his answers did hint at some kind of change of direction. “Laurent [Blanc] was Laurent, Didier was Didier, and Zizou is Zizou,” he said playfully.

One of Zidane’s long-term objectives will be to compete with the reigning world champions, who have now beaten France in three consecutive tournament semi‑finals. “I spent 25 years in Spain and you know what that means,” he said, before pointing out that the task ahead went beyond beating La Roja. “I know Spanish football very well, but they won’t be the only opponents. You have to beat all of the teams.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

View image in fullscreen Zinedine Zidane was sent off by Horazio Elizondo for butting Italy’s Marco Materazzi in the chest in the 2006 World Cup final. Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The Guardian

Zidane’s four-year contract will begin next month, with his extended staff to be unveiled a few weeks before the first internationals of the new season. “We’ll see each other again in September to talk about it. It’s a good thing that we’ll have three weeks with the players.” The focus for now, Zidane said, is on his first match in charge, which will be in Turkey on 25 September.

His homecoming, meanwhile, will be against Italy, just over 20 years after his dramatic exit from the international stage. If the raucous reception as he stepped out of the FFF headquarters is anything to go by, it will be one of the more memorable evenings in the Stade de France’s history.

Sports.title: Roberto Mancini returns as Italy head coach with Claudio Ranieri named technical director
Sports.content:
Roberto Mancini has agreed to be Italy head coach for a second time, the president of the Italian Football ​Federation (FIGC), Giovanni Malagò, said on Tuesday, also confirming Claudio Ranieri would take over as technical director.

Mancini replaces Gennaro Gattuso, who ⁠left the post in April after Italy failed to qualify for a third World Cup in succession, and returns to a job he held between 2018 and 2023. He led the national team to European Championship glory in 2021 with a penalty shootout victory over England at Wembley but then failed to reach the 2022 World Cup and a slow start to Euro 2024 qualifying. In total, Mancini managed Italy for 58 matches during his first spell and at club level has managed Inter, Fiorentina and Manchester City, where he spent three years and guided them to their first Premier League title in 2011-12.

“Mancini is the coach,” Malago ‌said on Tuesday. “I believed that the best person to become head coach was ‌Roberto Mancini.”

The former FIGC technical director ‌Paolo Maldini and his adviser, Leonardo, resigned from their roles on Monday after Andrea Pirlo’s appointment as head coach was blocked because of the former midfielder’s ties to a Russian betting firm. Pep Guardiola was the association’s first choice but turned down the job last month.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Ranieri replaces ⁠Maldini. The 74-year-old, who led Leicester City to the Premier League title in ​2016, will oversee technical operations and ​elite football development across Italy’s national team structures. “I needed someone with ​whom I could share ‌the decision on ​the coach, because ​without that shared view my reasoning would have carried little weight,” Malago said. “So consequently, we have a new coach and a new technical director for Italy.”

Sports.title: Shirtless Tom Brady enjoys family vacation to Alaska as NFL icon and his three children pose with sled dogs and go fishing on 'trip of a lifetime'
Sports.content:
Tom Brady and his three children enjoyed 'the trip of a lifetime' in Alaska in recent days as the NFL icon posted a series of loving pictures from their vacation.

The seven-time Super Bowl winner, 48, posted a flurry of images from the fun-filled trip on Instagram on Tuesday.

Brady flew west with his daughter Vivian, 13, and sons Jack, 18 and Benjamin, 16, for a few days of adventure in the outdoors.

The pictures show the Brady clan enjoying a trip with a pack of sled dogs, while they also went fishing in lakes and were brave enough to go swimming in the icy water overlooked by stunning mountains.

Brady made sure to get a snap of his ripped physique within the post as he bravely took off his shirt and jumped off the side of a boat into the bitterly cold water.

'A week in Alaska with my three best friends. The trip of a lifetime,' Brady wrote in his caption, along with a heart emoji.

Tom Brady and his three children enjoyed 'the trip of a lifetime' in Alaska in recent days

Brady bravely took of his shirt and jumped off the side of a boat into the bitterly cold water

The seven-time Super Bowl champion poses with sons Jack and Benjamin on a boat

It continued what has been a busy summer for Brady. He attended Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce's lavish New York City wedding earlier this month, watched plenty of World Cup action and even squeezed in a golf trip to Ireland with his dad.

But the legendary quarterback has also attracted plenty of criticism in recent weeks for starting a dramatic feud with Logan Paul.

Amid the spectacle of the World Cup final between champions Spain and Argentina in New York, the NFL legend flipped his middle finger at Paul in the latest stunt.

A day earlier Brady slapped YouTuber-turned-wrestler Paul at a Fanatics Fest event in New York. The saga began with the pair's flag football 'feud' earlier this year.

A source suggested to The Daily Mail that the 'feud' with Brady and Paul is 'expected to eventually spill over into the WWE ring' at some point in the future.

Many fear Brady, 48, is having a midlife crisis, amplified by the wounds of his divorce from supermodel Gisele Bundchen in 2022 after 13 years of marriage.

Things are only going to get busier for the former New England Patriots and Tampa Bay Buccaneers star when the new NFL season gets underway in a matter of weeks.

Brady is poised to enter the third year of his decade-long, $375 million contract as Fox's lead NFL color commentator.

He's also juggling his responsibilities as a minority owner with the Las Vegas Raiders and, on Tuesday, his head coach Klint Kubiak announced Kirk Cousins would be the starting quarterback in training camp.

Pictures show the Brady clan enjoying a trip with a pack of sled dogs in glorious surroundings

They seemed to spend plenty of time outdoors and enjoyed a successful fishing trip

That means Brady's No. 1 NFL Draft pick, Indiana Hoosiers national champion Fernando Mendoza, is already down the depth chart.

Brady shares Vivian and Benjamin with ex-wife Gisele. He shares Jack with ex-girlfriend Bridget Moynahan.

Despite their separations, Brady appears to maintain a good relationship with his exes, wishing them both a happy Mother's Day earlier this year.

Brady and Bundchen split in 2022 and the Brazilian supermodel has gone on to have another child with current partner Joaquim Valente.

Moynahan and Brady were never married but instead learned they were having a baby after splitting up in late 2006.

Sports.title: LIV Golf's demise accelerates as $40m season finale is 'set to be CANCELED'... but players are still in the dark about future
Sports.content:
LIV Golf's demise accelerates as $40m season finale is 'set to be CANCELED'... but players are still in the dark about future

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

LIV Golf is set to cancel its season-ending team championship tournament in what may be the death knell for the Saudi-backed rebel tour.

The event, LIV Golf Michigan, was set to be held in suburban Detroit at The Cardinal at Saint John's Resort from August 27-30 and had a prize pool of $40million.

But sources tell FrontOfficeSports that an announcement will be made on Wednesday officially confirming the cancellation of the 2026 showpiece.

The cancellation comes as the future of the rebel tour that pried names like Jon Rahm, Cameron Smith, and Bryson DeChambeau from the PGA Tour remains in question after the Saudi PIF announced it would stop funding LIV after this season's end.

In the months since that announcement, players have been left somewhat in the dark over the viability for the future of the circuit.

Rumors surrounding the cancellation of the LIV regular-season finale - LIV Golf Indianapolis - also continue to be bandied about. However, that event is still scheduled to take place from August 20-23.

LIV Golf is set to cancel its team championship event with its $40m prize pool

The rebel tour, which poached Cam Smith (L) and Bryson DeChambeau (R), is seemingly on its last legs after the Saudi PIF announced plans to pull its funding at the conclusion of the season

The tour now needs to raise $350million to operate a season in 2027 after the PIF's exit

But the Michigan event seems destined for the chopping block. One source told FOS last month, 'I don't think they'll ever get to Michigan.'

Around the same time, LIV CEO Scott O'Neil couldn't guarantee that all four remaining events would go on as scheduled. One of those four events, LIV Golf UK, did get played.

Hints were dropped last week by Martin Kaymer, the captain of LIV's Cleeks GC team, who told Today's Golfer the Michigan team championship was 'highly unlikely' to be played after O'Neil held a captains meeting that left 'lingering questions' to be answered.

The final three events were scheduled to take place in the United States. In addition to the Indianapolis event, LIV Golf New York is still scheduled to go on at Trump National Golf Club in Bedminster, New Jersey.

Of the $40million prize pool, the winning squad was supposed to take home $11.2million. Both those figures are down from last year's numbers of $50m and $14m, respectively.

This is the second event to be cancelled this season, joining LIV Golf Louisiana's cancellation from back in April.

LIV is still looking for new investors to replace the funding from the PIF. The tour is hoping to raise up to $350million to keep the league running in 2027.

Sports.title: Man City's forgotten man Kalvin Phillips is set for ANOTHER loan move after being left out of Man City squad for Asia tour - with injured Jack Grealish also absent
Sports.content:
Kalvin Phillips is finalising a new loan move to Sheffield United after being left off Manchester City's squad list to tour Asia.

As Daily Mail Sport revealed last month, Chris Wilder is keen to re-sign the 30-year-old, who has two years left on his contract, despite a difficult loan spell last season.

Phillips made just three appearances for Sheffield United last term and was sent off on his last appearance for the club in the Steel City derby win over Sheffield Wednesday.

Phillips has endured a torrid time since joining City for £42 million from Leeds United and is keen to kickstart his career.

The 30-year-old former England international was desperate to make an impact, but his lack of games in recent seasons and subsequent shortage of match sharpness put him at a physical disadvantage.

The 31-cap international previously had loan spells with West Ham and Ipswich in the Premier League before linking up with Sheffield United in January.

Phillips made just three appearances for Sheffield United last term and was sent off on his last appearance for the club in the Steel City derby win over Sheffield Wednesday

Including his loan moves, he has made a total of 46 league appearances since joining City almost four years ago.

Talking to BBC Radio Sheffield towards the end of the season, Wilder said: 'He'll have a lot of people still after him. We've brought a really good pro in. He was unlucky with his injury and he's not played as much as he wanted to play.

MAN CITY TOUR SQUAD

Goalkeepers Gianluigi Donnarumma, Marcus Bettinelli, Max Chabot, Jack Wint. Defenders Rayan Ait-Nouri, Max Alleyne, Kaden Braithwaite, Josko Gvardiol, Matty Henderson-Hall, Abdukodir Khusanov, Rico Lewis, Stephen Mfuni, Vitor Reis. Midfielders Claudio Echeverri, Phil Foden, Jaden Heskey, Mateo Kovacic, Jeremy Monga, Divine Mukasa, Nico Gonzalez, Xavier Parker, Tijjani Reijnders, Floyd Samba, Antoine Semenyo, Savinho. Forwards Mahamadou Sangare, Divin Mubama, Ryan McAidoo.

'I spoke to him and said we'd love to be an option for you, your agent and your parent club if that is a possibility.

'He certainly ticks the box in terms of personality and characteristics, off the pitch and on it. If there's an opportunity I'm sure we'll try and explore that one.'

Jack Grealish has also been left out of City's pre-season tour as he continues his rehabilitation and individual training programme.

Grealish joined Everton on loan at the beginning of last season and his time with the Toffees got off to the perfect start as he notched two goals and six assists during the early months of the season.

But in January the attacker suffered a stress fracture during a game against his former club Aston Villa, which required surgery.

The injury marked the end of Grealish's season – and thereby killed his World Cup hopes - and he stayed at the Hill Dickinson club until the end of the season to undergo his rehabilitation.

He has since returned to City, posting a picture of himself on the grass last week with the caption: 'Nice to see everyone, am nearly there! Hopefully not long now till back training for good'.

There has been interest from Saudi Arabia - and Everton are also aware of his situation - but a decision on his future looks likely to come later in the window.

Savinho also wants to push through his move to Tottenham but City maintain his valuation has not been met and would want a replacement before they allow the 22-year-old to leave.

Sources at Tottenham indicate City's valuation has changed since initial talks.

City have considered the likes of Ibrahim Mbaye from PSG and Chelsea's Pedro Neto as potential wing additions.

Sports.title: Silver lining for England's 'sexy and aggressive' track Goddess: Amy Hunt misses out on Commonwealth Games gold in women's 100m final
Sports.content:
As Amy Hunt paraded through the interview room, a beaming smile and the English flag draped over her drenched shoulders, she wiggled her fingers to flash her silver rings.

‘I need to start wearing gold jewellery,’ she laughed, having just finished second in the 100 metres final. There was no shame whatsoever in her silver medal, but Hunt has always been one of life’s over achievers.

‘If anyone wants to buy some gold rings for me, that would be amazing!’ added the Cambridge University graduate.

She lost three of her acrylic nails on the starting blocks. The conditions in Glasgow were filthy, splashing and dashing through torrential rain to finish in a time of 10.98 seconds.

‘It was pretty gross on the start line,’ she said. ‘My fingers were underwater but you just have to roll with the punches at champs.’

Throughout the evening, stadium staff pushed giant squeegee machines over the surface to soak up the water. They absorb 60 litres per minute but nothing could prevent the track from turning into a 100m slip and slide.

Amy Hunt sprinted to silver in the women's 100m final at the Commonwealth Games

New Zealand's Zoe Hobbs made a fast start to the final and held off Hunt to claim the gold

Hunt, seen congratulating Hobbs, has view this all as part of her long-term project building towards the Los Angeles 2028 Olympic Games

Billy Connolly was born 15 minutes away this stadium, which is usually occupied by the Glasgow Warriors rugby team. As the city’s windswept comedian once said: ‘There are two seasons in Scotland: June and winter.’

Outside of Scotstoun, volunteers were determined not to be brought down by the washout. ‘No Scotland, no party,’ they chanted. In the uncovered stand behind the finish line, most of the party had left for shelter by the time Hunt crossed the line.

For Hunt, you suspect this is all part of a long-term project to put her in medal contention for the 200m at the 2028 Olympics. The 24-year-old has been working hard to improve her start - and it was her top-end speed pulled her back into the medal positions. So far in 2026, Hunt has set personal bests over 50, 60 and 100 metres. It will all help improve her chances the warmer climates of Los Angeles.

Here, however, it Zoe Hobbs of New Zealand won gold, surprising the field from Lane 7.

‘I had a really terrible first 60 metres,’ said Hunt. ‘So I think it just shows the calibre of my top end speed that I could dig myself out of the horrendous ditch that I dug in the first half of the race.

‘It was the first 10 for me. I'm a legitimate starter. I can get it right, and today I got it really badly wrong. My top end speed is so formidable that I was able to claw back that silver but I think gold was definitely there for the taking. I beat Zoe in the semis - and she's an incredible athlete. She ran a PB to win, but I think gold was definitely there.’

Heather Oakes was the last woman to win 100m gold for England in the Commonwealths. That was back in 1986, when 32 nations boycotted the competition because Margaret Thatcher refused to impose sanctions on South Africa's apartheid government. The wait goes on.

Many of the world’s fastest women stayed away from Glasgow this week. Olympic champion Julien Alfred, of St Lucia, was among the absentees, along with the British Virgin Islands’ Adaejah Hodge, who has clocked the fastest time in the world this year. You suspect they were not full of regret when they turned on their TV sets to see athletes huddled under umbrellas. The high jump was delayed for almost two hours.

Englishman Elliot Jones raced earlier in the evening, losing out in his 100m semi-final. The 28-year-old needed to wring out his running spikes as he headed back into the changing room. ‘There was water all over the lane,’ said Jones, who watched Cameroonian Emmanuel Eseme win the final with a Games record time of 9.83s.

‘It felt like I couldn't get any traction. I didn't feel like I was moving anywhere. It's frustrating, but everyone's got the same conditions. I got in the blocks and I was pushing water out my lanes. In between the false start and the start, the water had repoured. It's a Scottish summer, isn't it?’

This was a summer headline that Hunt was not prepared to miss out on. Her parents travelled up from Newark to watch, booking an Airbnb with her coach. Only the Commonwealths? Tell that to her mentor, the double gold medallist Darren Campbell.

‘I think it's really, really important as a track athlete,’ said Hunt, who won 200m silver in the World Championships in Tokyo last September. ‘We don't get much representation in terms of media. We're not NBA players. We're not on TV three times a week, when everyone's seeing our faces.

‘It's really, really important in terms of my journey as an athlete, my legacy is an athlete. I don't want to go on my Wikipedia page in 30 years' time and just see one or two medals. I want to see lists and lists of medals. This is my first Commonwealth Games, so it was really good to come here.’

And the Glaswegian storm clouds, at least, had a silver lining.

Sports.title: UEFA lay into FIFA over 'proposal to sell stakes in the World Cup' in a move that could 'make president Gianni Infantino millions' - as plan is labelled a 'nuclear bomb' for football
Sports.content:
UEFA lay into FIFA over 'proposal to sell stakes in the World Cup' in a move that could 'make president Gianni Infantino millions' - as plan is labelled a 'nuclear bomb' for football

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

UEFA have hit out at a leaked FIFA plan to sell stakes in the World Cup in a move that could make its president Gianni Infantino millions.

News broke in The Times on Tuesday afternoon that FIFA boss Infantino was considering selling parts of the tournament to private investors and forming a new company in a deal that could be worth around £15billion.

The report added that Infantino could become the commissioner of that company once his role at FIFA ends in 2031, a highly lucrative position that estimates suggest could pay him more than $50million-a-year.

The bank JPMorgan is said to be handling the process and the Donald Trump administration is understood to have been consulted.

The proposal has already received widespread criticism from across football, with one source telling The Times it would be a 'nuclear bomb' for the sport and another arguing it would 'potentially be much worse than the European Super League'.

It is understood the English FA were completely unaware of the proposal.

And UEFA, which has been critical of FIFA and Infantino's actions in recent times, hit out at the plans.

FIFA are reportedly planning to sell stakes in the World Cup in a hugely contentious move

UEFA launched a strongly worded statement slamming plans that 'crossed a line' (pictured - UEFA President Aleksander Ceferin)

'This crosses a line that football’s governing institutions should never cross,' they said in a statement. 'UEFA takes it extremely seriously. So should every National Football Association.

'So should every stakeholder: leagues, clubs, players, supporters, governments and everyone who cares about the future of the game.

'The soul and governance of football are not assets to trade - especially with zero transparency as to who gains financially. None of us are the owners of football. It is not FIFA’s to sell.'

Former FIFA president Sepp Blatter also condemned the governing body's reported plan.

'The close relationship between the FIFA President and the US President has reached a financial dimension that is deeply damaging football,' Blatter wrote on X.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham also hit out at FIFA on social media, writing: 'No one has the right to sell our game.'

'Let me say this very directly. Football does not belong to investors. It belongs to the people who fill the stands and who stand on the touchline week in, week out, rain or shine.

'The World Cup is not a product. It is the greatest competition in world sport, and it was never anyone's to sell.

'Dress the deal up however you like. Once you have sold a piece of it, you have sold out. Football belongs to the fans. It always has, and it always will.'

If the move was to go ahead, the global football calendar would likely be affected.

For example, the Men's and Women's World Cup may be expanded or held more regularly than every four years, while the Club World Cup could face similar changes.

Joshua Kushner, the brother of Donald Trump's son-in-law Jared, was reported to be one of the potential investors

As part of the proposal, all 211 member associations would have stakes that would make up 20 per cent of the total company and be worth around $20million (£15million) each.

That is a larger figure than many of their annual revenues, and they would be given the option to sell them to raise funds.

FIFA would retain a majority stake in the new entity and private investors would be able to take on minority stakes.

FIFA are a not-for-profit organisation and enjoy tax-free status at their HQ in Switzerland.

For the most recent cycle of 2022-2026, their revenue is expected to be around $15billion (£11.3billion) – much of which came from this summer's World Cup – meaning this would provide a lucrative opportunity for individuals to be involved in.

The Times added that the blueprint for the potential selling of stakes has been discussed among senior FIFA figures and potential investors, which could include Joshua Kushner, the brother of Trump’s son-in-law Jared – and they have signed non-disclosure agreements.

Some of those potential investors are understood to have even spoken internally about 'buying FIFA'.

Infantino's proposed new role could be extremely lucrative. Figures close to the plan are said to see it on a par with the NFL, whose commissioner Roger Goodell earns about $64million a year.

The reports come at a time when Infantino is already under fire for a variety of reasons following the World Cup.

This includes the US visa restrictions that affected supporters and officials from many countries, the extremely high prices of tickets and Infantino's links with Trump, which came to a head after Folarin Balogun's red card was suspended following a phone call by the US President to the Swiss administrator.

When contacted for comment, FIFA confirmed plans to launch a new body called FIFA Forward Enterprise, which they described as a 'controlled subsidiary consolidating FIFA's commercial and event operations'.

They added that 'FIFA would retain sole control of FFE and exclusive authority over football governance, competitions, match calendar, and all regulatory and sporting decisions,' and claimed the move would increase the funding available to all 211 member associations.

The Daily Mail Sport also contacted the White House for comment.

Sports.title: Man United open to offers for FOUR academy graduates, Newcastle insist Arsenal have not made approach for Bruno Guimaraes, Nottingham Forest among list of clubs targeting Chelsea's Liam Delap: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
Man United open to offers for FOUR academy graduates, Newcastle insist Arsenal have not made approach for Bruno Guimaraes, Nottingham Forest among list of clubs targeting Chelsea's Liam Delap: WINDOW WATCH

It's that time of the year again - the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period with clubs looking to make big signings ahead of next season.

Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...

Sky Blues near club-record £22.5m deal for Rushworth

Coventry City are closing on a £22.5million deal for Brighton goalkeeper Carl Rushworth.

Add ons will take the fee closer to £30m and a sell-on percentage will also be included.

A medical is being scheduled for later this week for the 25-year-old who also attracted interest from Newcastle United.

Coventry City are closing on a £22.5m deal for 25-year-old Brighton goalkeeper Carl Rushworth, who also attracted interest from Newcastle United

Bees line up Henderson replacement

Brentford are advancing in talks to sign Lens midfielder Mamadou Sangare as a potential replacement for Jordan Henderson.

The Bees have been talking to Lens for a couple of months about the Mali international in a deal that could be worth £40million, though they have faced competition from Crystal Palace who are managed by Sangare's former coach Pierre Sage.

The 24-year-old is keen on the move to the Premier League and Brentford hope to finalise terms ahead of their London rivals, with Henderson due to join Chelsea on a free transfer.

Brentford want two midfielders and are also weighing up a move for Tottenham midfielder Pape Matar Sarr.

They remain in talks over 18-year-old Ousmane Diabete from Genclirbirligi, amid competition from Spurs, but the teenager is regarded as one for the future.

Sarr, 23, has had interest from Turkey but would be open to remaining in London if, as it seems, his first-team starting chances will be limited following Spurs' purchase of Sandro Tonali and Mateus Fernandes.

Brentford want two midfielders and are also weighing up a move for Tottenham midfielder Pape Matar Sarr

Fulham's Palacios talks continue

Fulham have held further talks over a deal for Real Madrid midfielder Cesar Palacios.

The 21-year-old made his debut for the senior team in January and is well known to Fulham boss Alvaro Arbeloa, who is keen to bring the Spain Under 20 international and forward Gonzalo Garcia to London from his former club.

Arokodare passes Ajax medical

Wolves striker Tolu Arokodare has passed his medical with Ajax.

The 25-year-old has also completed the paperwork on his loan with Ajax having the option to buy Arokodare for £17m.

The Dutch club will pay a £1m loan fee, with add-ons, if they reach the league phase of a European competition.

The 25-year-old has also completed the paperwork on his loan with Ajax having the option to buy Arokodare for £17m

United youngsters attracting attention

Manchester United are open to offers for Harry Amass, Dan Gore, Toby Collyer and Radek Vitek.

Several clubs have already made enquiries for goalkeeper Vitek and left-back Amass for loans and permanent deals while Gore and Collyer could also go on loan.

They will continue to train with the first team until other members of the squad re-join following their break for the World Cup.

However, their regular game time after that is more likely to come with the club's U21s so United are looking for them to gain more competitive action elsewhere.

Several clubs have already made enquiries for goalkeeper Vitek and left-back Amass (left) for loans and permanent deals

Stones set for Inter medical

Inter Milan are expecting John Stones to undergo a medical on Thursday is ahead of his move to Italy.

The England international and his representatives are finalising terms over a free transfer and a two-year deal.

The 32-year-old is a free agent after leaving Manchester City and Inter are progressing in talks for Christian Romero from Spurs also.

Meanwhile, Chelsea defender Benoit Badiashile and West Ham's Jean-Clair Todibo are on Napoli's list as the Serie A side work on signing a new centre back.

John Stones is set for a medical at Inter Milan as he prepares to join on a free transfer

Phillips edges closer to Blades return

Kalvin Phillips is finalising a new loan move to Sheffield United after being left off Manchester City’s squad list to tour Asia.

As Daily Mail Sport revealed last month, Chris Wilder is keen to re-sign the 30-year-old - who has two years left on his contract - despite a difficult loan spell last season.

Phillips made just three appearances for Sheffield United last term and was sent off on his last appearance for the club in the Steel City derby win over Sheffield Wednesday.

Phillips has endured a torrid time since joining City for £42million from Leeds United and is keen to kickstart his career.

Manchester City's Kalvin Phillips is on the verge of re-joining Championship Sheffield United

Black Cats zero in on Methalie

Sunderland are continuing talks over a potential £26million deal for left-back Dayann Methalie from Toulouse.

As Daily Mail Sport previously reported, the France Under 21 international defender, who can also operate as a centre-back, emerged as a Sunderland target after previously attracting interest from Newcastle United.

But Regis Le Bris is hopeful Sunderland can bring him in on a five-year contract for what would be a record sale for Toulouse.

Dayann Methalie (right) emerged as a Sunderland target after previously attracting interest from Newcastle

Forest putting out feelers for Famalicao's Sa

Nottingham Forest are in talks to sign Portuguese attacking midfielder Gustavo Sa from Famalicao.

The 21-year-old was a target for Saudi Arabian clubs earlier in the year and West Ham this summer but Forest may now sign him and then send on loan to Olympiacos.

Sa was the captain of Famalicao last season, scoring four goals and claiming two assists from 34 appearances.

Tomiyasu training with Palace

Former Arsenal defender Takehiro Tomiyasu is training with Crystal Palace after the expiry of his contract at Ajax.

The Japan international was expected to extend his contract but is a free agent after making just nine appearances since moving to Amsterdam on a short-term deal in January owing in part to a hamstring injury.

The 27-year-old is training with Palace in Como as part of the club’s pre-season preparations and could feature in a friendly this week. He has had interest from Venezia and Sassuolu, too.

Palace are playing in the Como Cup. They face Lens, new manager Pierre Sage's former side, tonight then take on Famalicao in two 45-minute games.

Takehiro Tomiyasu

Bees eye Sarr signing

Brentford are weighing up a move for Tottenham midfielder Pape Matar Sarr.

The Bees were looking to strengthen their options even before news of Jordan Henderson's proposed departure for Chelsea.

They remain in talks over 18-year-old Ousmane Diabate from Genclirbirligi, amid competition from Spurs, but the teenager is regarded as one for the future. They now want two more for the first team squad with Henderson heading towards Stamford Bridge.

Sarr, 23, has had interest from Turkey but would be open to remaining in London if, as it seems, his first team starting chances will be limited following Spurs' purchase of Sandro Tonali and Mateus Fernandes.

Pape Matar Sarr is on Brentford's radar, with Jordan Henderson wanted by Chelsea

Newcastle still waiting on Arsenal bid for Bruno

Newcastle United insist they have still to receive a formal approach from Arsenal for midfielder Bruno Guimaraes.

Arsenal have been preparing to make an official £70m-plus move for the Brazilian who is keen to join them but, so far, Newcastle sources say any proposals have come via the player's agent.

Newcastle manager Eddie Howe said at the weekend he was unsure what would happen over the 28-year-old's future.

Bruno Guimaraes wants to move to Arsenal but Newcastle say they are still waiting for a bid

Delap in demand with Chelsea set to sign Welbeck

Nottingham Forest remain among the list of clubs showing interest in Chelsea striker Liam Delap.

Danny Welbeck's pending arrival from Brighton is likely to leave fewer opportunities for 22-year-old Delap and clubs are enquiring to ascertain the deal required to sign the former Ipswich Town forward.

Forest, Everton and Newcastle United are just some of the clubs who have expressed interest in the former England U21 international.

Meanwhile, Forest have made an offer for Union Saint-Gilloise full-back Anan Khalaili as talks for Feyenoord's Givairo Read also continue.

Both players are also appreciated by Bournemouth and Newcastle United.

Liam Delap is a target for several clubs with his chances at Chelsea likely to be limited

Jorgensen leaves camp for France

Chelsea goalkeeper Filip Jorgensen has left their camp in Australia ahead of joining sister club Strasbourg.

The 24-year-old Denmark international made 12 appearances for Chelsea last season and wants regular first team football.

On my Edson! Ajax want West Ham's Alvarez back

Ajax are trying to re-sign West Ham midfielder Edson Alvarez.

The Dutch side sold Alvarez to West Ham for £35million in 2023 and now hope to buy him back.

West Ham want around £12.5m but Ajax sources say they are still owed money from the way payment was structured on the original transfer.

The 28-year-old, who has spoken to Ajax director Jordi Cruyff, spent last season on loan at Fenerbahce and was part of Mexico's World Cup squad but has generally struggled to live up to expectations since leaving Amsterdam.

Real Sociedad are also interested in Alvarez but are proposing a smaller, structured deal.

Edson Alvarez in action for Mexico against England at the World Cup

Rock on Tommi to Meadow Lane

Aston Villa winger Tommi O'Reilly is in talks to join League One Notts County on loan.

The 22-year-old had been set to sign for Sheffield Wednesday but, after further discussions, Villa have decided Meadow Lane may suit his development better.

O'Reilly had an outstanding campaign with Crewe last season and Villa hope he can replicate that form under Notts County coach Martin Paterson.

Notts County also signed Australian forward Luka Smyth from Finnish top-flight side VPS yesterday for an undisclosed fee on a three-year deal.

Notts County are in talks over a deal for Villa's Tommi O'Reilly

Perri set for Italian job after Trafford deal

Leeds United goalkeeper Lucas Perri is expected to join Torino on loan with an option to buy once a deal for James Trafford is completed.

Trafford, 23, is poised to sign a deal worth around £130,000 a week once Manchester City and Leeds finalise details on an expected £40m transfer with £5m in add-ons and a sell-on clause.

Torino and Leeds have agreed an initial loan move for Perri for the coming season. The deal also includes an option to buy him permanently next summer.

Leeds goalkeepers Karl Darlow and Illan Meslier have left Daniel Farke’s squad to join Manchester United and Arsenal this summer.

They would still like another as cover as well as strengthening at left-back, attacking midfield and striker.

Lucas Perri's Torino deal may be signed off after James Trafford arrives from Manchester City

Real Madrid are set to hold contract talks with Vinicius Jr, with Arsenal still interested

Sports.title: Village cricket rocked by cheating allegation after Saltburn's clash with Norton
Sports.content:
Village cricket rocked by cheating allegation after Saltburn's clash with Norton

An investigation has now been launched into Saltburn’s 2nd XI cricket match with Norton in Division Two of the North Yorkshire and South Durham League

View 2 Images A village cricket game is being investigated

Village cricket has been rocked by a cheating scandal after a fielder was accused of clicking his fingers to mimic the sound of the ball hitting the bat.

‌



Footage appears to show a slip fielder for Saltburn 2nd XI snapping his fingers just before his wicketkeeper takes a catch. The batter appears confused to be given out.

‌



After the clip circulated, people accused him of fooling the umpire into thinking the batter had edged the ball.

‌



Ben Mummery, who shared the footage on social media, said: "Click-gate has gone viral and I’m genuinely really happy it’s being exposed. Harshest possible punishment please. It’s not cricket."

England cricket icon says wife was left 'suicidal' over Azeem Rafiq racism storm READ MORE :

View 2 Images An investigation has been launched into Saltburn’s match with Norton after cheating allegations (Image: Saltburn CC)

‌



The incident happened in a match in the North Yorkshire and South Durham League (NYSDL) between Saltburn 2nd XI and Norton 2nd XI, while ­Saltburn were fielding.

League leaders Saltburn ended up winning by a huge margin of 159 runs at their home ground in North Yorkshire.

Rory Cotterill, who captained Middlesbrough CC’s 2nd XI in a 29-run defeat to Saltburn in June, has since claimed a similar situation occurred in that match. He shared a video online which allegedly showed the same player clicking his fingers.

Article continues below

The NYSDL confirmed it received a formal complaint regarding S­aturday’s game.

It said: “A full investigation has been initiated and until such time as the formal processes are complete no further comment will be made.”

Saltburn CC has been approached for comment.

Sports.title: Xabi Alonso drops telling hint over Chelsea’s Jordan Henderson and Danny Welbeck transfers
Sports.content:
Xabi Alonso drops telling hint over Chelsea’s Jordan Henderson and Danny Welbeck transfers

Chelsea have been linked with moves for veteran Premier League stars Jordan Henderson and Danny Welbeck and boss Xabi Alonso has spoken out on deals for the pair

View 2 Images Xabi Alonso took charge of his first Chelsea match on Tuesday (Image: Getty Images)

Xabi Alonso has refused to confirm Chelsea are interested in signing Danny Welbeck and Jordan Henderson - but hinted that the Blues want to add more experience. The Blues have been linked with moves for the veteran stars over the past few days.

‌



Reports have suggested that Henderson, 36, will be allowed to leave Brentford on a free transfer just a year after moving to West London. It has also been suggested that Chelsea are already in talks with Brighton regarding a move for Welbeck.

‌



Asked about potential deals following Tuesday’s 6-4 victory against Western Sydney Wanderers, new Chelsea boss Alonso remained tight-lipped.

‌



He said: “No, I'm sure that from today until the last day of the transfer [window] there will be a lot of rumours, so to be commenting on all of them. It's going to be a hard task, but for sure we need proper balance in terms of qualities, in terms of positions, in terms of balance.

“We want to have a complete squad and we want to make a good team. For that we have an idea, we have a plan and let's see how we set it up until the start of the Premier League.”

Chelsea hoping to repeat Man Utd and Liverpool's inspired transfer deals with latest moves READ MORE :

Xabi Alonso left with easy transfer decision as Chelsea win Western Sydney Wanderers goalfest READ MORE :

Chelsea’s moves for Henderson and Welbeck are huge departures from their previous approach in the market. Having preferred to sign youth with promise in previous windows, the Londoners now appear to be prioritising experience.

‌



Chelsea have of course already been busy in the window this summer. Morgan Rogers arrived from Aston Villa for £117m earlier this summer, while Marco Palestra was signed from Atalanta.

Elsewhere, Geovany Quenda and Emmanuel Emegha arrived at Stamford Bridge on pre-agreed moves. The Blues have already earned considerable sums back, with Andrey Santos and Marc Cucurella having joined Manchester United and Real Madrid respectively.

View 2 Images Chelsea are interested in signing Jordan Henderson (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Tyrique George has signed permanently for Everton following last season’s loan spell, while Alejandro Garnacho has been allowed to move to Aston Villa on loan. Another star who could leave before the end of the transfer window is striker Liam Delap.

The 23-year-old endured a difficult debut season with Chelsea, having netted on just three occasions. On the striker, Alonso added: “Every player that is involved is doing well, Liam as well. It was 60 minutes when he had to battle hard against the centre-backs, a good few lays off, so he's doing well and preparing for the season.

“I see him in a good mood, in a good desire to get proper fitness, proper football feeling good, and he's doing well.”
