World.title: Historic drought: Paks NPP output cut, Romanian NPP reactor offline due to River Danube’s low water level
World.content:
The government has made preparations if any steps are needed to ensure Hungary’s secure energy supply, Economy and Energy Minister István Kapitány said in a post on Facebook on Tuesday. Kapitány acknowledged a cut in the output of the Paks nuclear power plant. Furthermore, Romania has taken one of the reactors at its Cernavodă nuclear power station offline because of the exceptionally low water levels in the Danube

Kapitány acknowledged a cut in the output of the Paks nuclear power plant due to record-low water levels on the Danube, which the NPP uses for cooling, and warned that another heatwave could arrive in Europe in the coming days, boosting demand for electricity even as water levels fall further.

“We have prepared for this situation,” he said, adding that the ministry is in constant contact with the Paks NPP, transmission system operator MAVIR and state-owned energy company MVM.

“We have held professional-level consultations and are assessing developments from hour to hour,” he said. “We are managing the situation in a responsible and transparent manner, in compliance with all professional norms,” he added. Kapitány said the public would be updated on any important developments.

The Paks NPP said it cut output of its number 1 block by 254 MW in the evening on Monday as water levels on the Danube reached -106cm.

Danube reaches record low in Budapest

An all-time record low water level in the River Danube of 31 centimetres was registered in central Budapest on Tuesday morning, breaking an earlier record of 33 centimetres, the water management directorate (OVF) reported. The authority noted that all Europe’s rivers are critically low.

Another heat dome approaches Hungary while the Danube reaches historic low water levels. Photo: Facebook/Valyo, város és a folyó

Romania shuts down nuclear reactor as Danube runs low

Romania has taken one of the reactors at its Cernavodă nuclear power station offline because of the exceptionally low water levels in the Danube, the plant’s operator said on Tuesday.

State-owned Nuclearelectrica said the No 1 reactor had been disconnected from the national grid and shut down because of severe drought and the river’s reduced flow. The Danube provides cooling water for the plant, and its discharge has fallen to an unprecedented level in the past three decades. The lowest reading, 1,750 cubic metres a second, was recorded on 16 July.

The end draws near for Lake Velence as Danube hits a record low in Budapest: will Hungary dry out this year?

Nuclearelectrica said it was in постоян contact with the authorities responsible for water management and would not rule out shutting down the second reactor, depending on how river levels develop. At present, the No 1 unit is not expected to restart before 4 August at the earliest.

Romania’s only nuclear power station first went into operation in 1996. The plant, near Cernavodă on the Danube close to the Black Sea, has two reactors built using Canadian Candu technology and together they generate about 20 percent of the country’s electricity.

World.title: Video: Ferocious storm slams Hungary, ripping up trees as if they were tomato stakes
World.content:
A rarely seen, gale-force windstorm has torn through north-eastern Hungary, Transcarpathia, and the north-western and eastern regions of Romania and Slovakia. The cold front that passed quietly and almost dry across much of Hungary yesterday wreaked considerable damage in these areas. Here are some of the images and footage.

Ferocious storm slams Hungary

Fülesd is a small village of fewer than 400 inhabitants in Szabolcs-Szatmár-Bereg county, close to both the Hungarian–Romanian and Hungarian–Ukrainian borders. It was here that yesterday’s devastating, tornado-like windstorm struck, sweeping away large trees as if they were mere tomato stakes. In nearby Kispalád, a hailstorm of a kind not seen for many years battered the village, with walnut-sized hailstones falling everywhere.

As we also reported, yesterday a moderate cold front reached Hungary and raced across the Carpathian Basin, but it did not bring significant rainfall. In north-eastern Hungary and eastern Slovakia, however, it developed into a chain of thunderstorms that ripped through these regions, bringing hail, tornado-like winds and relatively large amounts of sudden torrential rain. In Fülesd, a recently published video suggests that a short-lived whirlwind may also have formed.

Hail fell in Mikota and Tiszakóród. According to idokep.hu, these chunks of ice were lifted up and down repeatedly within the thundercloud for a long period.

One eyewitness said he had never seen anything so frightening, as the gale-force winds toppled trees one after another and tore roofs from residential buildings. You can watch the terrifying footage below:

In the area around Csenger, Csengerújfalu and Tyukod a striking funnel cloud formed, although this is not connected with the possible tornado in Fülesd, as that occurred later. Here are some of the pictures:

Over Uzhhorod, the storm arrived with brutal hail:

Transcarpathia power supply cut

Across the region, the storm caused severe damage. According to MTI, in Transcarpathia power supply has been completely cut in 38 settlements and partially disrupted in a further 64, as a result of Monday’s late-afternoon storm, which in places was accompanied by hailstones the size of walnuts.

Another brutal heat dome arrives as Danube nears record low — what to expect this week

According to the Kárpáti Igaz Szó news portal, in the district centred on Berehove, which is largely populated by ethnic Hungarians, the worst damage was suffered by Bene, Makkosjánosi and Sárosoroszi, where the roofs of family homes, several schools and kindergartens were damaged.

Meteorology: capital’s wind record broken on Monday

The capital’s wind record was broken on Monday, HungaroMet Zrt. reported on its website on Tuesday. It said that on János Hill in Budapest, instruments measured winds of 85 kilometres per hour in the early afternoon’s storm, beating the previous daily record for the strongest gust in the capital. The earlier record for this date was 83 kilometres per hour, also measured on János Hill, in 2019.

World.title: Video: Century-old Ford Model T takes centre stage at Hungarian National Museum
World.content:
A 100-year-old Ford Model T has arrived at the Hungarian National Museum, where it was carefully lifted by crane and wheeled into the building under strict conservation measures on Monday morning. The historic vehicle will feature in the museum’s upcoming exhibition, The American Dream, opening to the public on Thursday, the museum noted.

Ford Model T in the Hungarian National Museum

The Ford Model T, a centrepiece of the Transport Museum’s collection, holds special significance as its design involved two Hungarian engineers, József Galamb and Jenő Farkas. Curators Klára Radnóti and Angelika Orgona chose to include it in the exhibition to highlight this connection. The car, exactly a century old this year, boasts a 3,500cc engine with 18 horsepower and remains fully operational.

The American Dream exhibition, marking the 250th anniversary of US independence, will showcase not only the Ford Model T but also a wealth of fascinating artefacts. At its heart, the exhibition explores the lives of Hungarians who emigrated to America, alongside the stories of famous figures who spent time in the US, including Lajos Kossuth, Albert Szent-Györgyi, Zsazsa Gábor, and Zita Szeleczky, with personal mementoes on display.

The American Dream – Hungarians in the United States, 1776–2026 will run from 30 July to 1 November.

World.title: Scandal, if true: PM Orbán’s former deputy and opposition KDNP party head Zsolt Semjén accused of raping a minor by victim
World.content:
Sándor Bangó, a former resident of the Szőlő Street correctional institution, had previously only hinted that he had been raped as a child in the institution by a senior politician. In the early hours of this morning, however, he named the man in question: Zsolt Semjén, Hungary’s former Deputy PM and opposition Christian KDNP’s chairman. Although his post carries an ominous message, according to Péter Juhász, former Együtt-politician and Bangó’s representative, he is well, and anyone wishing him well should not try to contact him now.

The “Uncle Zsolti” allegation emerges

Bangó Sándor’s name is not new to Hungarian public life, nor is the “Uncle Zsolti” figure he has now identified. It was Gábor Kuslits, former director of Budapest’s child protection service, who first mentioned in an interview with Válasz Online that Péter Juhász Pál, the former director of the Szőlő Street correctional institution, had been protected by two senior politicians. In return, boys were “supplied” to one of them and girls to the other. Kuslits, however, admitted in the interview that this was nothing more than unchecked hearsay.

Hidden camera footage from the Szőlő Street juvenile detention centre. Photo: PrtScr/Youtube

After that, Péter Juhász, formerly of Együtt, a Hungarian liberal party, published a video about the Ózd children’s home, where, according to János Látó, who describes himself as a pastor, a senior politician had been visiting for sexual purposes. Látó said this to him on the basis of what two boys brought up there had told him, one of whom referred to the man as Uncle Zsolti. Juhász also suggested that this story could not be proven. It later emerged that Látó’s credibility was, at the very least, questionable, Telex reports.

Protest at the Szőlő Street juvenile detention centre. Photo: Facebook/Klára Dobrev

János Látó speaks in Kossuth Square:

Nevertheless, the Uncle Zsolti allegation has irreversibly entered public consciousness, and DK’s Gergely Arató immediately questioned then deputy prime minister Zsolt Semjén about it. He dismissed it as a “Beelzebub allegation” and rejected even the implication. To this day, no one has succeeded in finding evidence for Uncle Zsolti’s existence or identity.

The former Szőlő Street resident speaks out

Bangó Sándor gave an interview to Kontroll, close to Márton Magyar, the brother of Prime Minister Péter Magyar, on 24 April. In it, he said he had entered the institution at the age of 14 or 15, and claimed that Péter Juhász Pál repeatedly raped him and then prostituted him, including to Uncle Zsolti. On the basis of this testimony, he became the key witness in proceedings against Péter Juhász Pál.

Sándor Bangó. Screenshot: Kontroll

He said the incidents took place in the dark, but on one occasion, when he switched on the light, he also saw the perpetrator’s face. He even named the man to the editorial staff, but they did not make it public because of the investigation.

A “senior politician”: the key witness in the Szőlő Street abuse case has come forward

Two weeks later, Bangó gave testimony at the Budapest Regional Investigative Prosecutor’s Office, where he said he identified Uncle Zsolti and declared that he would also undergo a lie detector test. This did not happen, however, because of his mental state, which immediately raises legitimate questions about his claims.

He revealed who Uncle Zsolti is — but can he be believed?

At the time, he also said that on 9 July, when he left for America, he would reveal publicly who Uncle Zsolti was. According to him, he did not do so at the firm request of the prosecution.

But something seems to have happened, because in the early hours of this morning he posted on his TikTok page that Uncle Zsolti is none other than Zsolt Semjén, Orbán Viktor’s former deputy prime minister and leader of the KDNP. Fidesz-KDNP immediately issued a statement describing the claim as an absurd lie, obvious political manipulation and defamation. In their view, Bangó is himself a victim, but the gravest responsibility therefore lies not with him, but with his “political exploiters and instigators”. On Tuesday morning, several KDNP MPs posted Facebook messages with the same wording, saying: “We stand by Zsolt Semjén! Zsolt Semjén is innocent!”

Zsolt Semjén last weekend at Tusványos festival with former PM Viktor Orbán. Photo: Facebook/Semjén Zsolt

World.title: British investor Ghai Sant Ram acquires plot near Bucharest for new residential project
World.content:
British investor Ghai Sant Ram announced the purchase of a plot of approximately 30,000 square meters from fiery Romanian businessman and football club owner George Becali on Tuesday, July 28.

The purchase price was approximately EUR 14.3 million, and the land was acquired together with the building permit for a large-scale real estate development. The transaction was brokered by CGA Home Consulting through Cătălin Apetri (right), the company’s CEO and founder, who also serves as Romania Development Director for Ghai Family Holding and Ghai Sant Ram.

The plot located near Pipera Plaza, northern Bucharest, was acquired via Ghai Family Holding. The investor intends to develop a residential project comprising approximately 650 apartments on the newly acquired land.

“The Pipera area, where the newly acquired plot is located, has genuine residential demand, driven both by northern Bucharest’s business hub and by rapid access to infrastructure, services, schools and shopping centers. The area’s long-term potential underpins our decision to invest here in a new residential development comprising 650 apartments,” said Cătălin Apetri, CEO and founder of CGA Home Consulting and Romania Development Director for Ghai Family Holding.

Ghai Sant Ram has more than two decades of experience in residential development across the United Kingdom and Romania. The British investor previously developed Ivory Residence and Horizon City in Romania.

Details of the new development’s exact configuration, apartment mix, number of parking spaces, amenities, total investment value and construction timetable will be announced once the technical stages have been completed.

The plot's “location provides easy access both to central Bucharest and to Voluntari, Tunari, DN1, the Bucharest Ring Road and the A3 motorway. Proximity to Tei Park and Herăstrău Park is another major advantage, while the location is also relevant for families working in northern Bucharest,” said Cristian Stanciu (left), CEO of the Ivory Residence and Horizon City residential projects.

With the 650 new apartments planned on the plot, Ghai Sant Ram’s residential portfolio in Romania will exceed 2,500 units overall.

World.title: PwC: Bucharest Stock Exchange capitalization exceeded EUR 100 bln for first time in history in 2025
World.content:
The market capitalization of the Bucharest Stock Exchange exceeded the EUR 100 billion threshold (RON 537.7 billion) for the first time in its history at the end of 2025, the highest level in the past 19 years, and growth accelerated in 2026, according to the ninth edition of the PwC Romania report “Bucharest Stock Exchange and M&A valuation multiples.”

The Regulated Market accounted for RON 523.7 billion, up by 49% compared to 2024, while the MTS/AeRO segment reached RON 14.6 billion, up by 15%. The BET index increased by 46% in 2025, to 24,439 points, its best annual performance since 2009, while the BET-TR index, which also reflects the dividends paid by its constituent companies, advanced by 55%, to 57,230 points, ranking among the top-performing equity indices globally.

“2025 was a landmark year for the local capital market. Despite a backdrop marked by a large budget deficit, the highest inflation rate in the European Union and persistent geopolitical tensions, the BET index delivered its best annual performance in 16 years, and market capitalization exceeded EUR 100 billion for the first time. MSCI’s reclassification of Romania as an Advanced Frontier Market in June 2025, along with FTSE Russell’s confirmation of 14 Romanian companies in its global indices, shows that international investors’ interest in the local market is strengthening,” said Sorin Petre, Leader of the Valuation and Economics department at PwC Romania.

2025 and the first part of 2026 brought three initial public offerings that were large by the standards of the local capital market, alongside several smaller transactions. The three major deals completed were: Cris-Tim Family Holding (RON 454 million, 42x oversubscription, November 2025), Electro-Alfa International (RON 579.6 million, 60x oversubscription, March 2026) and Christian ’76 Tour (RON 149 million, June 2026).

The number of active retail investors on the BVB grew from 226,000 at the end of 2024 to over 285,000 at the end of 2025, an increase of 26% and four times the level recorded in 2020.

“Although market capitalization grew by 49% in 2025, traded value decreased slightly, by 1%, which shows that the strong appreciation in prices was not matched by a similar rise in trading activity, with liquidity remaining concentrated in a limited number of issuers,” added Sorin Petre.

The five most traded shares on the Regulated Market in 2025 were Banca Transilvania (28% of total traded value), OMV Petrom, Hidroelectrica, Aquila Part Prod Com and Romgaz, together accounting for 58% of total traded value. As in previous years, they belonged to the financial services, Oil & Gas and Electricity sectors.

The average return of the capital market, more than the risk-free rate, which rewards investors for taking on higher risk, was 7.6% for the BET index and 15.3% for the BET-TR index over the period 2015–2025.

In 2025, the excess return reached 37% for BET and 45% for BET-TR, against a risk-free rate of 6.8%. Romania’s equity market capitalisation to GDP ratio stood at 27.7% as of 31 December 2025, higher than in previous years but still below the levels observed in other regional markets such as Greece, Croatia, and Hungary.

The number of BVB-listed companies with ESG scores reached 24 at the end of 2025, with a combined market capitalisation of RON 280.8 billion. Companies in the Oil & Gas, Electricity and Financial services sectors account for approximately 90% of the capitalisation of the companies with an ESG score.

With a significantly larger number of listed companies (331) and a total capitalization of EUR 105.5 billion, companies listed on the BVB remain on average smaller than those listed on markets such as Poland, Greece or Czechia, which positions the BVB as a mid-sized market in the region.

The local bond market also reached a record level in 2025, with total issuance of EUR 6.3 billion (RON 31.8 billion), almost three times the 2022 level, mostly generated by government bonds. Corporate issuance rebounded strongly, to EUR 2 billion, the highest level in the analysed period. In 2025, 27 out of the 33 corporate bond listings were carried out exclusively on international markets.

In 2025, the median EBITDA multiple of the companies listed on the BVB main market was 9.7x, while on the AeRO Premium segment it stood at 9.0x. The average EBITDA multiple derived from the analysis of transactions completed on the local market in 2025 was 7.6x, below the historical average of 8.2x. The gap might be explained by the fact that companies listed on the BVB are generally perceived as more stable, whereas private transactions often involve companies valued based on their future growth prospects.

On the Regulated Market, the highest median P/E multiple was recorded by the Consumer and Healthcare sectors (20.6x) and by IT&C (17.8x), whereas the lowest levels were observed in the Real estate (7.6x) and financial services (7.9x) sectors. The aggregate median P/E multiple was 12.7x in 2025, above the average of the last 19 years (11.2x).

World.title: Timișoara City Celebration expands accessibility with sign language concerts, inclusive spaces
World.content:
This year's Timișoara City Celebration will expand accessibility measures for people with hearing impairments and neurodiverse visitors, with sign language interpretation at several headline concerts and dedicated viewing areas. The event will take place between July 31 and August 3.

The organizers said concerts by Beth Hart, The Script, Irina Rimes, and Alexandra Căpitănescu will be interpreted into Romanian Sign Language (LSR), continuing an initiative first introduced during Timișoara's 2023 European Capital of Culture program and maintained in subsequent editions of the festival.

Romanian Sign Language interpretation will be provided by Denis Blidariu, an interpreter who has worked at concerts, festivals, theaters, cinemas, and international conferences.

The main stage area will also include a dedicated viewing platform for neurodiverse visitors, designed to provide a more comfortable concert experience and improved visibility. A separate area will be available for people with hearing impairments.

The accessibility measures are part of a broader effort by the Timișoara Project Center, one of the event's organizers, to make public cultural events more inclusive.

The 2026 edition of Timișoara City Celebration will be held under the theme "One city. A thousand ways to experience it. Diversity.”

World.title: Four bears to be transferred from Romania's Libearty Sanctuary to wildlife park in France
World.content:
Four rescued brown bears from Romania's Libearty Sanctuary in Zărnești will be relocated to a wildlife park in France as part of an international conservation partnership, Agerpres reported. The transfer, involving four young sibling bears, was described by the sanctuary's operator as an unprecedented operation for Romania.

The Millions of Friends Association (AMP), which manages the sanctuary, said the bears, named Alexandra, Anita, Chance, and Thomas, are about two and a half years old and were rescued from the wild.

They will be transported by road to Parc Animalier de Sainte-Croix after being sedated, with the journey expected to take more than a day.

“Four bears rescued from the wild and now in our care will leave Romania together for a park in France. […] It is an unprecedented transfer for AMP Libearty and a unique event for Romania," the association said.

According to AMP, as quoted by the news agency, the relocation has been planned in detail to ensure the animals' safety throughout the journey.

The organization said that the French park shares a similar vision focused on wildlife conservation and environmental education.

Parc Animalier de Sainte-Croix spans 120 hectares and is home to around 1,500 animals from 100 European wildlife species. In addition to its conservation work, the park offers visitors the opportunity to stay overnight in cabins within the park and observe the animals from close range, according to Agerpres.

World.title: IT tops sectors in Romania with highest salaries despite layoffs
World.content:
IT remained the field with the highest salaries on the Romanian market in the first half of 2026, despite the contraction in hiring volumes and even layoffs in profile companies. Salaries in the sector averaged RON 8,000, up by 5% compared to last year, according to Salario data, the salary comparator operated by eJobs.

The second best-paid sector on the market was oil and gas, with a net average of RON 7,000, followed by research and development, at RON 6,800. All three sectors were also featured in the ranking of the best-paying fields last year.

The following industries were construction/installations (RON 6,500) and engineering, telecommunications, audit/consultancy, and naval/aeronautics, each with RON 6,000 net per month on average.

“Even though in most fields we are talking about salary increases compared with last year, in real terms employees’ purchasing power has decreased, including in the sectors where salaries increased the most, because the increases were, in most cases, even half the level of inflation. In June, the inflation rate was 10.4%,” said Roxana Drăghici, Head of Sales at eJobs, the largest online recruitment platform in Romania.

Salario data showed that employees’ expectations exceeded the salaries they received by 30% on average. The largest differences were in IT, where the salary expectations expressed by candidates were 50% higher than those offered by employers. As such, employees in this sector expected an average of RON 11,993.

The insurance sector showed differences of 42%, while the automotive industry, legal and banking sectors showed differences of 40%.

By comparison, employees in the oil and gas sector expected an average salary of RON 9,000, compared to the actual salary average, RON 7,000. In alternative medicine, the difference was only 14%, in sanitary installations 20%, and in customer relations 25%.

Data also showed that among the fields with the lowest salaries are the industries that bring the largest number of jobs to the market, namely retail, services, the food industry, and tourism. The average net salaries for these sectors were RON 4,300 for retail, RON 4,500 for the food industry, RON 4,400 for call-center/BPO, RON 5,000 for transport/logistics, and RON 5,500 for services.

The field with the lowest salaries, however, is au pair/babysitting/cleaning, with RON 3,300 per month.

According to official data, in May the average salary in the Romanian economy reached RON 5,684, up by 3.2% compared with May 2025.

World.title: Revolut opens private market funds to retail investors in Romania
World.content:
Revolut said that it launched access to private market funds for individual investors in Romania, allowing eligible customers to invest in private equity, private credit, and infrastructure assets through its app. The funds are managed by Apollo, Ares, Hamilton Lane, and Partners Group and are structured under the European Union’s ELTIF 2.0 framework.

Private market investments have traditionally been dominated by institutional investors, partly because minimum commitments can exceed EUR 100,000 and because products often involve complex documentation, capital calls, and long lock-up periods.

Revolut said the new offering is aimed at experienced investors with a long-term investment horizon and is intended to lower some of those entry barriers. Management and performance fees may apply.

The four asset managers included in the initial offering collectively manage or oversee more than USD 2.8 trillion in assets, according to the fintech company. Revolut said its internal fund selection team assesses each product’s strategy, performance history, operational resilience, and ability to withstand different market cycles.

“For a long time, private markets have been missing from the average investor’s portfolio, not because of a lack of interest, but because of a lack of access,” said Rolandas Juteika, Revolut’s head of wealth and trading for the European Economic Area. “By partnering with firms such as Apollo, Ares, Hamilton Lane, and Partners Group, we are changing that dynamic.”

The funds will use the ELTIF 2.0 structure, which was designed to broaden access to long-term investments across the EU. The products offered through Revolut will be evergreen funds, meaning investors can put money into an existing portfolio rather than waiting for capital to be deployed gradually.

However, the company warned that the investments remain fundamentally illiquid despite offering periodic redemption windows. Withdrawals are not guaranteed and may be limited or suspended under the terms of each fund.

“These funds are deliberately structured for long-term capital, reflecting the underlying nature of private assets,” Juteika said.

Revolut said investors should be prepared to hold the products for several years and should only allocate a small portion of their overall portfolio to an ELTIF.

World.title: Colombia to close embassy in Romania shortly after reopening it
World.content:
Colombia’s president-elect, Abelardo de la Espriella, announced on Sunday, July 26, that his administration, which will take office on August 7, will close at least 14 embassies, including the one in Romania, as part of a reorganization of the country’s diplomatic network.

Earlier this year, during the mandate of the current president of the South American country, Gustavo Petro, Colombia had reopened its embassy in Romania after 24 years of direct diplomatic absence between the two states.

The new president presented another course regarding the embassies. “In a first stage, I will close the embassies in Algeria, Azerbaijan, Barbados, Cuba, the Czech Republic, Ethiopia, Ghana, Haiti, Hungary, Malaysia, Nicaragua, Romania, Senegal, and South Africa,” De la Espriella said in a speech on his social media accounts in which he also announced the suspension of the opening of the mission in Palestine, according to Euronews English.

De la Espriella assured that these measures “do not mean the severing of diplomatic relations” with the affected countries, except for Cuba and Nicaragua, arguing that “there will be no link with tyrannies.”

Instead, the president-elect explained that Colombian citizens in the countries where embassies will be closed will continue to receive assistance through the concurrent representation of other diplomatic missions in the region and that the reorganization aims “to make the foreign service more efficient.”

As part of this strategy, Abelardo de la Espriella also announced the reopening of Colombia’s Embassy in Israel, which will operate in Jerusalem, a promise the new president made during the presidential campaign, and the opening of a diplomatic mission in Nigeria, to reorganize the South American country’s presence in Africa.

He also indicated that he will unify some diplomatic representations which, in his opinion, “duplicate their functions,” such as Colombia’s embassies in France and at UNESCO in Paris, as well as those in Italy and at the United Nations Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) in Rome, so that a single ambassador will assume both representations.

The president-elect added that within the first 100 days of his government, he will request a technical audit of the remaining diplomatic representations in order to assess their continuity and stated that the resources saved through these measures will be used to strengthen sectors such as security, health, education, and infrastructure.

World.title: Schönbrunn Palace Orchestra Vienna to perform in Romania during Imperial Christmas Gala
World.content:
The famed Schönbrunn Palace Orchestra Vienna is set to return to Bucharest and perform at the Romanian Athenaeum on December 20 for the Imperial Christmas Gala, an event that has reached its 7th edition.

The evening's repertoire will bring together famous waltzes, lively polkas and emblematic musical pages by Johann Strauss II, alongside other jewels of Viennese classical music.

“Returning to Bucharest every December is for us a gesture of continuity and artistic affection. Imperial Christmas Gala has become a symbol of the meeting between Viennese tradition and an extraordinarily receptive and cultivated audience. It is our way of saying thank you for a year that is coming to an end,” said Peter Hosek, manager of Schönbrunn Palace Orchestra Vienna, according to Eventim.

Tickets for the event start at RON 329 (EUR 63) and can go to RON 629 (EUR 120).

Founded in 1997, Schönbrunn Palace Orchestra Vienna performs concerts at the Orangery of Schönbrunn Palace, at the Vienna State Opera and at prestigious festivals in Salzburg, being constantly invited to important stages around the world: Sweden, Finland, Germany, Italy, Romania, Japan, China and the United States.

Devoted to the Viennese tradition, the orchestra performs Johann Strauss waltzes, creations by Mozart, Haydn and Schubert, as well as works dedicated to festive moments.

In recent years, Schönbrunn Palace Orchestra Vienna has consolidated its status as an ambassador of authentic Viennese style through extensive international tours and appearances on increasingly diverse stages, from Europe to Asia and overseas. The orchestra is famous for the homogeneity of its sound, stylistic precision and stage elegance.

World.title: Montenegro Approves Paid Leave for Menstrual Pain Sufferers
World.content:
Rights groups have expressed satisfaction after Montenegro’s parliament amended the Health Insurance Law for women diagnosed with secondary dysmenorrhea – painful menstrual cramps – to grant two days of “menstrual leave” per month.

The measure, adopted by MPs on Monday, applies to women suffering such symptoms as a result of serious underlying conditions such as endometriosis, uterine fibroids, endometrial polyps, ovarian inflammation and polycystic ovary syndrome.

The initiative was submitted in March ahead of International Women’s Day by independent MP Jevrosima Pejovic. The bill previously received support from the parliamentary Health, Labour and Social Welfare Committee and the Legislative Committee.

The Women’s Rights Centre, an NGO, welcomed the adoption of paid menstrual leave, describing it as an important step toward recognising women’s health needs in the workplace. It also praised the persistence of MP Pejovic, who advocated for the measure.

“This is a valuable example of how the presence of women in politics helps give political significance to women’s experiences, which have long been pushed into the private sphere and treated as ‘secondary’ issues,” the NGO said on Tuesday.

The Centre recalled that it had proposed including this right into law two years ago, but the relevant ministry rejected the initiative at the time. “What matters now is that it does not remain merely a right on paper but becomes a concrete opportunity that provides women with safer, healthier and more dignified working conditions,” it said.

According to the explanatory note accompanying the legislation, the amendments are intended to properly regulate diagnosed pathological conditions, eliminate prejudice against women in the workplace and help balance their health needs with professional obligations.

The law defines the condition as symptoms caused by previously diagnosed gynecological disorders and lists symptoms including pain in intercourse, painful urination, infertility and unusually heavy menstrual bleeding. Diagnosis must be confirmed by a medical specialist.

Women seeking the new benefit will be required to renew their medical certificate by December 31 each year and submit it to their employer by January 30 of the following year.

The amendments also regulate compensation during leave. Under Montenegro’s Health Insurance Law, compensation for temporary incapacity for work is generally set at no less than 70 per cent of the salary base, while employers may provide a higher amount through collective agreements.

The law provides 100 per cent compensation for certain categories of illness and medical conditions, including occupational diseases and injuries, pregnancy-related complications, malignant diseases, haemophilia, cystic fibrosis, epilepsy, muscular dystrophy, cerebral palsy, paraplegia and quadriplegia, systemic autoimmune diseases, chronic renal failure requiring dialysis, HIV, psychoses and some other serious conditions.

The amendments do not say how the law will be implemented, including how employers and state institutions will verify eligibility and prevent possible abuses of the new entitlement.

BIRN was unable to reach MP Pejovic for comment on implementation of the law and safeguards against potential misuse.

The amendments are expected to enter into force after their publication in Montenegro’s Official Gazette.

World.title: Mayor Acquitted of Obstructing Justice in Kosovo War Crimes Trial
World.content:
This post is also available in this language: Shqip Bos/Hrv/Srp



The defendants celebrate the acquittal at Pristina Basic Court, July 28, 2026. Photo: BIRN.

Pristina Basic Court cleared local wartime commander Sami Lushtaku and seven others on Tuesday of obstruction of justice, witness intimidation and participation in a criminal group.

Sami Lushtaku, a commander in the Kosovo Liberation Army, KLA, for the region of Drenica, was accused of having from 2013 until 2015 forced two defendants to change their testimonies in the so-called Drenica case, in which Lushtaku and other KLA commanders from the Drenica region were accused of committing war crimes.

Lushtaku was not present when the judge announced the verdict, which was applauded by the public in the courtroom.

“The court could not find any convincing evidence which would prove the guilt of the defendants,” Judge Leon Perlaska said, reading the verdict. “The court assessed the testimony of the witness codenamed ‘Witness C’ where he denied that he was forced to change his statement,” Perlaska added.

Lushtaku, now mayor of the Kosovo town of Skenderaj/Srbica, was sentenced in 2015 to 12 years in prison by the Basic Court in Mitrovica for a murder committed in 1998, although the victim’s name was unknown and no body was found.

He was cleared on appeal in 2016 but his conviction for “command responsibility for allegedly violating the [bodily] integrity and health of an undefined number of civilian Albanians held at the Likovc detention centre” was upheld.

His sentence was reduced from 12 to seven years in prison by the Appeals Court. He was cleared by the Supreme Court in July 2017.

World.title: Kosovo Retrial Confirms Serbian Police Ex-Inspector’s Ten-Year Sentence
World.content:
This post is also available in this language: Shqip Bos/Hrv/Srp



Sacir Lutvija in court om July 28, 2026. Photo: BIRN.



Sacir Lutvija, a 65-year-old ethnic Gorani former member of the Serbian police force, was sentenced to ten years in prison in a retrial at the Pristina Basic Court, for war crimes committed during the 1998-99 war in Kosovo.

Serbian police and military forces staged a campaign of arrests of ethnic Albanian civilians and 11 of them were taken to Prizren police station in southern Kosovo, where Lutvija was among the inspectors who questioned them, according to the indictment.

Prosecutors said those arrested were beaten during the interrogation and subjected to electric shocks on their hands and genitals. One civilian died and ten others sustained serious injuries.

Lutvija, who has both Kosovo and Serbian citizenship, was arrested in October 2023 and has been in detention since then. The time in custody will be counted towards his sentence.

The Kosovo Special Prosecution charged Lutvija with unlawfully arresting and beating civilians, inhumane treatment and murder in his capacity as an inspector and police officer in Prizren. Lutvija pleaded not guilty in September last year.

Judge Kujtim Krasniqi on Tuesday ordered Lutvija to pay a court fee of 400 euros as well as 100 euros to the crime victims’ fund.

The verdict can be appealed.

Lutvija was initially sentenced to 10 years in prison by the Pristina Basic Court in November 2025.

But the Court of Appeals sent the case to a retrial in June this year having concluded that the Pristina Basic Court had not “concretely clarified the actions attributed to the accused in relation to each of the injured parties”.

The Court of Appeal also said the Basic Court failed to explained the accused’s participation in committing the crimes and “did not clarify the evidence upon which the conclusions presented in the verdict were based”.

The Gorani are a small Slavic ethnic group who mostly follow Islam and inhabit a highland triangle between Albania, Kosovo and North Macedonia.

World.title: Left High and Dry: Drought Exposes Central Europe’s Water Crisis
World.content:
Water management and retention

Described as the proverbial “roof of Europe”, Czechia sees all its rivers, streams and waterways flow out of the country – a systemic and geological drainage which makes the country particularly dependent on precipitation from above.

“This is a significant disadvantage, because most of the water we manage has to be retained: in the landscape, soil, hydrogeological structures or water reservoirs,” says Adam Vizina, head of the hydrology department at the Water Management Research Institute.

Water management and retention are, therefore, key for this landlocked country, yet the authorities appear short on solutions.

“Water will always flow away, but we can reduce our vulnerability,” argues Vizina, listing measures such as slowing runoff, interconnecting water supply systems, managing water reservoirs better, or protecting the quality and quantity of groundwater.

The state reportedly spent 75 billion crowns (about 3 billion euros) in the past three years on drought adaptation, yet experts – including a report by the Supreme Audit Office published last March – have criticised the slow pace and limited scope of the measures.

The Slovak Academy of Sciences recently released its “Vision for Slovakia 2040”, an extensive 90-page framework document commissioned by the government of Robert Fico laying out the key policy challenges for the next 15 years.

Among those, the forward-looking blueprint “identifies more frequent droughts as a key consequence of climate change and argues that strengthening water management, increasing landscape water retention and improving the resilience of agriculture and ecosystems should be central priorities for Slovakia’s long-term development.”

Whether the authorities will act on the recommendations is another matter, with experts long highlighting key shortcomings in Slovakia’s water management practices, from fragmented governance between different institutions and ministries, a lack of concrete follow-through, and scattered water data hindering real-time monitoring.

Czechia and Slovakia’s subpar water-management has deep roots dating back to decades of intensive farming that followed its collectivisation in the 1950s and 1960s under Communism – with all that entailed in terms of land consolidation, water erosion and reduced soil fertility, among other environmental impacts.

On the upside, the Czech Republic continues to receive roughly the same amount of rain on average every year as it used to, according to some estimates. But the way, time and place it does are changing, as must the measures meant to retain and manage it more effectively, experts say: less rainfall in the spring but more in the fall, more intense precipitation during storms, but less frequent episodes of long-term and widespread rain.

According to Milan Vitek from the local branch of Greenpeace, Czechia might soon be faced with the choice of keeping its scarce water either in the rivers or in its fields, but won’t be able to do both. “Adaptation is something that we are decades behind when we could’ve been much further ahead,” he previously told BIRN.

Water management or retention are also recently being cited as a silver bullet to solve Hungary’s problems. Although Hungary has a renewable water reservoir of 11,833 cubic metres per person, one of the largest in Central Europe (only Slovenia and Serbia have more in the region), 95 per cent of that originates from outside and simply flows through the country.

The building of dams or hydroelectric power plants has been a politically sensitive issue since the controversial plan to build the Bos-Nagymaros dam on the Danube helped trigger popular revolt against the Communist government in 1990. Since then, proposals for new dams and hydropower projects have remained politically off-limits in Hungary.

But times are changing. Laszlo Gajdos, the new Hungarian government’s environment minister, said at the height of the extreme heat at the beginning of July that “water is one of our most valuable resources for the future”.

Gajdos said the government must do everything it can to improve water retention, even with dam construction where necessary. “We should not let water flow through Hungary; it needs to be retained somehow. Personally, I don’t like this method, but it seems inevitable building some dams,” he told RTL.hu.

The government of Peter Magyar is working on a new climate and environmental law, expected by late autumn, which is set to address water management issues.

Gajdos, who became Hungary’s first environment minister in 16 years, stressed that water retention is a regional issue requiring cooperation with neighbouring countries.

Andras Szollosi-Nagy, who used to advise international organisations including the UN on water diplomacy and is the founder member of the World Water Council, could not agree more.

“Water retention is always somehow part of national sovereignty,” Szollosi-Nagy says. “The country upstream believes all the water is theirs, but if they retain it, neighbouring countries are affected. We need integrated water management in the region.”

He says there is no silver bullet to solve all the problems: dams, reservoirs, new technologies, satellite-based monitoring and controlled flooding could all play a role.

“Hungary’s water management system has been systematically dismantled in recent decades,” he says. “Now we need to rebuild it from scratch.”

World.title: Letter from Washington: US Seeks to Score Material Goals in the Balkans
World.content:
Greetings from America, which this month celebrated 250 years of independence from the British crown under a president who has called himself a king – and is also seen that way by the many thousands of people who have joined the “No Kings” protests in the US.

Donald Trump would not even allow the kings of football, the Spanish national team who won the World Cup, to enjoy their rightful moment on the throne this month. Instead, he lingered on stage after presenting them with the trophy at the stadium in New Jersey. An awkward situation was averted by Trump’s pal, FIFA President Gianni Infantino, who pulled the US leader aside, suggesting that it was time for him to step away.

Meanwhile, beside the footballing euphoria, the US-Iran memorandum of understanding has turned out to be more of a major misunderstanding. The war has escalated, bringing new American casualties and higher fuel prices, while reopening an uncomfortable question: what is the actual endgame? If the goal is to prevent Iran from developing nuclear weapons, to prevent further escalation in the Middle East, why is the United States simultaneously signing an agreement that would allow Saudi Arabia to develop the very same capability?

While all this has been happening, the Trump administration’s policy towards the Balkans has started to become increasingly clear. It is moving more aggressively into areas it considers important, such as energy, defence and infrastructure, while trying to push Russia, China and the European Union out of those spheres. Washington does not appear to be choosing its friends based on how developed their democracies are. Nor is it particularly troubled when someone in the Balkans talks about “ethnic cleansing”.

World.title: On Albania’s Adriatic Coast, Tourism Ambitions Put at Risk by Pollution
World.content:
Violeta was unimpressed by the rubbish blighting her summer holiday.

“It’s awful, isn’t it?” the 24-year-old said of the litter and construction waste strewn along beachfront at Golem Beach, a sandy stretch of Adriatic coast just south of the Albanian port city of Durres.

Golem is one of the most affordable holiday destinations in Albania, just 30 kilometres west of the capital, Tirana, and a relatively quick trip from neighbouring Kosovo. It is often packed with visitors, but Violeta said one week was enough.

“We’re going somewhere cleaner because of the pollution, like Ksamil,” she told BIRN, referring to a beach at the southern end of Albania. Pointing at rubbish, she said: “It bothers me because animals eat it and there are kids running around.”

World.title: What’s Driving the Real-Estate Price Surges in Eastern and South-East Europe?
World.content:
Rapidly rising real estate prices to the east and south of the Trieste-Szczecin line made existing dwelling owners happy - but potential buyers, especially younger people, less so.

According to Eurostat, in the first quarter of 2026, property prices in Bulgaria, Slovakia, and Croatia recorded price growth of 14 per cent over the first quarter of 2025. In a longer perspective of 3 and 10 years, the fortunes of individual countries have changed.

Generally, the total appreciation of housing real estate has been rapid, with Hungary in 10 years heading the list, followed by Bulgaria, Czechia, and Croatia.

However, Eurostat does not provide comparable data for countries southeast of Croatia, but Bosnia, Serbia, Montenegro, and others have followed similar paths. According to the Agency for Statistics of Bosnia, housing real estate prices increased by 20.4 per cent in the first quarter of 2026 compared to the first quarter of 2025. Nussubpekova recently reported a double-digit growth rate for Serbia.

World.title: North Macedonia Mourns Much-Loved Actor Goce Todorovski
World.content:
Goce Todorovski. Photo: Drama Theatre.

Actor Goce Todorovski has died aged 75, his family and the Drama Theatre in Skopje, where he spent most of his career, confirmed on Monday. The cause of death was not immediately announced.

Born in the western town of Kichevo in 1951, Todorovski graduated from the Faculty of Dramatic Arts in Skopje before joining the Drama Theatre in 1978. He went on to perform in more than 50 theatre productions, while also building a prolific career in television, radio and cinema.

His gift for comedy made him one of the country’s most enduring and popular actors.

For many Macedonians, Todorovski will be remembered above all for his appearances in the cult television series Macedonian Folk Tales (Makedonski Narodni Prikazni), whose humorous adaptations of traditional folklore became a fixture of family viewing for decades.

He was also a familiar face to generations of children through the educational television series “Scruffy Alphabet” (Bushava Azbuka), while radio audiences knew him from the long-running satirical comedy programme Hihiriku.

His film career included memorable roles in several classics of Macedonian and former Yugoslav cinema, including Happy New ’49 (Srekna Nova ’49), Weekend of the Dead (Vikend na Mrtovci), Trieste Via Skopje (Trst via Skopje), The Red Horse (Crveniot Konj), and many others.

Beyond his screen work, Todorovski was one of the leading comic actors of the Macedonian stage, collaborating with many of the country’s best-known theatre directors and helping shape the repertoire of the Drama Theatre for nearly five decades.

“Goce Todorovski never sought the audience’s affection. He won it from the moment he stepped onto the stage,” the Drama Theatre wrote in its farewell.

“His performances possessed a rare immediacy: a precise acting rhythm that seemed entirely effortless, expressive facial gestures, a distinctive stage presence, and the roguish charm with which he could effortlessly bridge the gap between the stage and the audience,” it said.

Todorovski’s performances earned numerous awards, including the state “23 October” prize for culture and the lifetime achievement award at the Vojdan Chernodrinski Theatre Festival in 2025, as well as the Presidential Order of Merit in 2023.

News of his death prompted an outpouring of tributes from fellow actors, public figures and audiences, many recalling the humour, warmth and distinctive characters that made Todorovski one of the defining faces of North Macedonia’s acting scene.

Actress Maja Andonovska Ilijevski wrote that Macedonian theatre had lost “a great man and a great actor”. Recalling their time filming the cult TV series Macedonian Folk Tales, she said Todorovski had been not only an acting legend but also a wonderful colleague, whose humour and warmth made those days unforgettable.

Andonovska said the countless characters Todorovski brought to life will remain part of the country’s collective memory, adding that “some people never truly leave – they live on through their roles, the memories of their colleagues and the love of their audience”.

Photographer Goran Anastasovski described Todorovski as “the man who made us laugh for decades” and “a giant on stage”, adding that his legacy of bringing smiles to various generations will endure.

World.title: Croatian Inspectors Step Up Crackdown on Illegal Holiday Rentals
World.content:
July the 29th, 2026 – Croatian inspectors have begun stepping up their crackdown on illegal holiday rentals up and down the coastline in particular, with plenty of fines already issued.

As Poslovni reports, Croatia’s State Inspectorate has intensified its inspections of holiday accommodation advertised on platforms such as Booking.com and Airbnb, targeting property owners who rent to tourists without meeting the country’s latest, strict legal requirements. The inspections form part of a broader effort to combat the shadow economy in the tourism sector and ensure fair competition among registered accommodation providers.

thousands of euros seized, thousands fined…

According to the State Inspectorate, inspectors have already uncovered numerous cases of illegal short-term rentals during this year’s tourist season. As a result, authorities have confiscated 343,000 euros in income believed to have been earned through unlawful renting, while fines imposed have exceeded 81,000 euros.

The inspections focus on identifying individuals advertising tourist accommodation without the required registration or operating in breach of Croatian tourism regulations. Authorities are checking online listings as well as conducting on-site inspections to verify whether accommodation providers comply with the law.

inspections will continue throughout summer

When inspectors discover illegal activity, they can issue fines, prohibit further renting and confiscate the financial gains obtained through unlawful operations. Officials say these measures are intended to discourage unregistered rentals and protect hosts who operate legally and meet all regulatory obligations. The State Inspectorate said inspections will continue throughout the peak summer tourist season, with online booking platforms remaining one of the primary tools used to identify suspected illegal accommodation.

Officials stress that the goal is not only to punish offenders but also to ensure equal market conditions, protect consumers and improve the overall quality and transparency of Croatia’s tourism sector. As demand for private accommodation continues to grow, authorities say stronger enforcement is necessary to prevent unfair competition and safeguard public revenue.

World.title: Airbnb Loses Its Advantage Over Booking.com for Croatian Hosts
World.content:
July the 29th, 2026 – Airbnb no longer has any advantages or particular benefits over Booking.com for Croatian hosts after the company announced significant changes recently.

As Ana Roksandic reports for Poslovni, Croatian private accommodation hosts are facing a significant changes after Airbnb announced a new commission model that many say removes one of its biggest advantages over Booking.com. Under that company’s new system, Airbnb will no longer charge guests a separate service fee. Instead, hosts will pay a 15.5% commission, replacing the previous model in which hosts paid around 3% while guests covered most of the platform’s fee.

According to Vedran Tomić, president of the Save Small Family Renters Association (SMOi), the change has been met with negative reactions from Croatian hosts. He said Airbnb’s biggest advantage had been its lower direct cost for hosts, but that will now disappear. He also pointed out that Croatian hosts must pay VAT on the commission, meaning they will now pay VAT on the full 15.5% fee instead of just the previous 3% commission.

one last summer of airbnb advantage for croatian hosts…

The new commission structure will apply as of the 13th of October. Airbnb says the change responds to feedback from hosts who found the previous pricing model confusing because guests saw an additional service fee added to the advertised accommodation price. Under the new model, guests will simply see the final price, while the commission is deducted from the host’s payout.

The changes come as Croatia’s short-term rental market is already evolving. Data from analytics platform AirDNA shows that the number of active listings has fallen in the country’s largest cities. In Split, active listings dropped from around 10,300 in June 2025 to 8,906 in June 2026, a decline of 13.5%. Zagreb recorded an even steeper fall of 25%, with analysts linking the decline to more property owners switching to long-term rentals. The market is increasingly favouring larger and more professional operators, while less profitable listings are leaving the sector.

Tomić believes the commission change is unlikely to reduce demand from travellers, but it could weaken Airbnb’s position in Croatia because it no longer offers hosts a financial advantage over Booking.com. He estimates that Booking.com controls around 70% of the Croatian market, while Airbnb accounts for roughly 20%, with the remaining 10% shared by other booking platforms.

accommodation competitiveness isn’t even the biggest issue for croatian tourism

Damir Krešić, director of Croatia’s Institute for Tourism, said higher commissions are not good news for the sector, but argued that accommodation is not the biggest competitiveness issue facing Croatian tourism. In his view, greater concerns are the rising costs of food, drinks and transport services, where Croatia has become less competitive.

Krešić also encouraged private hosts not to rely on a single booking platform. He said global platforms have given small Croatian hosts access to guests worldwide, but becoming too dependent on one intermediary weakens their bargaining position. Instead, he recommends that hosts advertise across two or three platforms to diversify their bookings and reduce risk.

World.title: Luka Modrić Visits Unfinished Villa Construction Site in Istria
World.content:
July the 29th, 2026 – Croatian footballing legend Luka Modrić has paid a visit to an unfinished villa construction site in Istria before heading off on a yacht. Could he be thinking of buying it?

As Poslovni reports, a jet black limousine with tinted rear windows stopped at a construction site in Istria a few days ago, shortly before midday. Luka Modrić, 40, captain of the Croatian national football team, got out at the parking area in front of an unfinished villa that still requires final stonework for a Mediterranean appearance.

He was accompanied by experts who went around the site with him explaining different things and pointing out important construction details. The group then entered the private property and remained inside for about half an hour. According to one of the site’s neighbours who contacted the media about the group, Luka Modrić appeared interested in the property as a possible investment, though that is not confirmed.

The same day he was later seen boarding a yacht that he rents each summer for roughly a week or ten days of family holiday along the Adriatic coastline. Media reports state that, after earlier investments in central Dalmatia and the far south of Croatia, members of the Modrić family have shown interest in property in Istria. Vanja Modrić is said to have expressed interest on several occasions in locations around Rovinj, but no purchases have so far been officially completed.

the football legend has acquired multiple properties in both croatia and spain

Over the course of his career Modrić has acquired several residential properties in Croatia and Spain.

In the elite Zadar suburb of Kožino, near where he grew up, the family owns a villa with an outdoor pool, children’s playground, garden, sea view, wine cellar, ten-car garage, gym, an eighteen-seat cinema, children’s playroom and massage room. It is used as a family base during the summer break in the football season. In October 2024 a storm damaged the access road; the damage was later repaired. The property had earlier attracted attention over reports of beach concreting in front of the estate; Modrić stated that the area in question is public land, not a private beach.

In Zagreb, the family owns a 286-square-metre villa on Pantovčak, purchased back in 2017 from former footballer Zvonimir Boban. Land-registry records show Modrić transferred ownership to his wife Vanja shortly afterwards. Before that purchase the family had lived in apartments in Ravnice and Babonićeva Street. Modrić also owns a 220-square-metre penthouse with a 29-square-metre loggia in a newly built building on Tkalčićeva Street in the city centre; media estimates placed its value at around 1.4 million euros.

Over in the Spanish capital of Madrid, where Luka Modrić spent many years playing for Real Madrid, the family owns a villa in the La Moraleja district, acquired in 2019 on a 10,000-square-metre plot. Spanish media describe it as having nine bedrooms and nine bathrooms, with the main living areas, kitchen and sitting room on the ground floor and guest rooms upstairs, plus an outdoor pool, garden and recreation space. According to media reports, part of the portfolio is formally registered in Vanja Modrić’s name.

World.title: Croatia Opens Its First Biological Swimming Pool in Čazma
World.content:
July the 29th, 2026 – Croatia has opened its very first biological swimming pool in the continental town of Čazma, representing a significant step forward in terms of sustainable tourism.

Croatia has officially opened its first biological swimming pool, marking a milestone in sustainable tourism and environmentally friendly recreation. Index reports that the new facility is located in the town of Čazma, around 60 kilometres east of Zagreb, the new facility is part of the much wider Čazma Natura project, which has the primary goal of transforming the town into a leading green tourism destination.

Unlike conventional swimming pools, the biological pool uses natural filtration instead of chlorine or other chemicals. Water is purified through biological processes involving aquatic plants and microorganisms, creating a safe swimming environment while preserving the natural ecosystem. It is the first public facility of its kind in Croatia.

The swimming area spans approximately 1,665 square metres and is divided into separate sections for swimmers and non-swimmers. Alongside the pool, visitors will find sunbathing areas, changing rooms, showers, a catering facility, children’s amenities and recreational spaces designed for families and visitors of all ages.

The pool forms part of the Bio Park Čazma complex, which also includes educational facilities, walking trails and nature-focused attractions. The project promotes sustainable tourism while highlighting the area’s biodiversity and encouraging visitors to explore the surrounding landscape.

Officials say the biological pool represents a new direction for Croatian tourism, combining recreation with environmental protection. Similar facilities have become increasingly popular across areas of Europe because they reduce chemical use, consume less energy and blend more naturally into their surroundings. With the opening of the country’s first biological swimming pool, Čazma is hoping to attract visitors looking for a different kind of summer experience, one centred on nature, sustainability and chemical-free swimming.

World.title: Croatian Firefighters Continue Battling Bordeaux Wildfire
World.content:
July the 28th, 2026 – Croatian firefighters are continuing to battle the intense Bordeaux wildfire ravaging southwestern France, and which keeps being rekindled by problematic winds.

Croatian Air Force firefighting pilots are continuing their mission in southwestern France, where they are helping battle the massive wildfire near Bordeaux. Index reports that this intense operation has now entered its fifth day, with crews facing increasingly difficult conditions as strengthening winds threaten to reignite areas that had previously been brought under control.

The members of the 855th Firefighting Squadron are operating in the Saumos area, just west of Bordeaux. According to Major Ivan Dukić, conditions improved after overnight rain, but rising temperatures and stronger afternoon winds have caused the fire to become active once again.

“The situation is much better than it initially was thanks to some rainfall. However, temperatures are increasing, and as the day progresses the wind is strengthening. The fire has been waking up again, so we’ll see what the days bring,” Dukić said from France.

Since arriving in France, the Croatian crews have carried out 118 flights, logged 20 hours of flying time, and dropped 576 tonnes of water on the catastrophic French wildfires. They are working alongside French and other international crews as part of the rescEU civil protection mechanism.

Despite the demanding mission abroad, Croatia’s aerial firefighting forces remain heavily engaged at home during the peak wildfire season. Between the 15th of June and the 27th of July, the 855th Firefighting Squadron took part in extinguishing 39 wildfires along Croatia’s coastline and on the islands.

Commander Colonel Željko Bukvić said Croatia’s ability to respond both domestically and internationally is the result of careful planning, good organisation and the experience of its firefighting crews. He stressed that the squadron remains ready to assist both Croatia and its European partners whenever needed. The enormous wildfire near Bordeaux remains one of France’s most serious emergencies, with strong, problematic winds, high temperatures and dry vegetation continuing to fuel the blaze repeatedly despite efforts. Croatian pilots remain on the front line as authorities work to prevent the fire from spreading further.

World.title: July 1377: Dubrovnik Introduces Organised Isolation of Arrivals to Combat Plague
World.content:
July the 28th, 2026 – Turning the clock back to July 1377, we saw how the ever-diplomatic Dubrovnik organised the isolation of new arrivals in order to combat the plague.

In July of the aforementioned year, the former Great Council of the Republic of Dubrovnik adopted a decision requiring people arriving in the city (and then autonomous state of Ragusa) from plague-affected areas to undergo a period of isolation before entering the city or its surroundings.

trentina – strict isolation for a period of one month

Dubrovnik was one of the most important medieval trading centres on the Adriatic. Its wealth depended on shipping, merchants and goods arriving from across the Mediterranean and the European hinterland. Those same connections also carried infectious diseases. After the Black Death swept through Europe in the mid-14th century and caused catastrophic issues, the authorities faced a clear problem. A complete ban on foreign arrivals and goods would have protected the population but would also have severely damaged an economy based on trade. Instead they introduced a compromise.

Arrivals from infected regions were not allowed to enter Dubrovnik immediately. Index writes that they had to spend a fixed period separated from the local population so that any symptoms of disease could appear. The initial isolation period lasted 30 days and was known as the “trentina”.

dubrovnik tried to stop the disease at the city gates

Isolation was carried out at Cavtat and on nearby islets such as Mrkan; later Bobara and Supetar were also used. The underlying principle was that a person who showed no signs of illness after a sufficiently long interval posed a substantially lower risk of introducing infection. Medieval physicians had absolutely no knowledge of the bacterium Yersinia pestis, which was identified much later at the very end of the 19th century. They did, however, observe from experience that the disease spread through contact and the movement of people, and that symptoms could appear only after a delay. Dubrovnik therefore tried to stop the disease at the gates rather than respond only after an outbreak inside the city.

Rules were strict. People from affected areas had to complete the prescribed isolation, and contact between Dubrovnik residents and those in isolation was limited, creating a sanitary buffer.

dubrovnik’s decision eventually became a global practice in epidemiology

The period was later extended from 30 to 40 days. The modern word “quarantine” derives from the Italian quaranta (forty). The precise reason for choosing 40 days is not certain; explanations range from medical observation to the symbolic importance of the number in Christian tradition.

In subsequent centuries Dubrovnik developed a more elaborate system, including lazarettos where travellers, merchants and goods could complete the required period of observation before entry. The arrangement allowed trade to continue under controlled conditions rather than forcing a choice between an open city exposed to disease and a completely closed one without commerce.

The 1377 decision is regarded as one of the earliest organised applications of a practice that later became a standard method of epidemic control worldwide.

World.title: Split is Launching One of Croatia’s Largest Environmental Projects
World.content:
July the 28th, 2026 – Split is set to launch one of Croatia’s largest environmental projects as part of a massive 100 million euro investment.

Poslovni reports that construction works on this enormous project will last 28 months from the contractor being introduced to the site until the start of the plant’s trial operation. The total duration of the contract itself is 43 months, including the trial operation period and obtaining the operating permit.

One of the most important infrastructure projects in Croatia’s water management sector is now beginning in Split. On Tuesday, the 28th July 2026, the start of construction works on the Stupe Wastewater Treatment Plant (UPOV Stupe) will be officially marked. The project is a key part of the “Improvement of Water and Utility Infrastructure of the Split–Solin Agglomeration” initiative.

With the expansion of the Stupe wastewater treatment plant, Split will receive a modern wastewater treatment system that, once completed, will become the second-largest wastewater treatment facility in all of Croatia and the central point of a unified sewage system serving the Split–Solin agglomeration.

The value of the contract for the design and expansion of the facility amounts to 99,056,751.25 euros including VAT. The works will be carried out by a consortium consisting of WTE Wassertechnik GmbH (lead partner) and HERING d.d.

The future facility will have a capacity of 275,000 population equivalents, with secondary biological wastewater treatment. The construction of the Stupe wastewater treatment plant will provide modern treatment of municipal wastewater for Split and the surrounding area, helping to further protect the environment, preserve the quality of the Brač Channel, and improve the quality of life for residents.

As part of the second phase of the project, eligible costs amount to 243,149,745.48 euros. Of this, €165,365,077.30 euros will be financed through non-refundable European Union funds from the Cohesion Fund, while the remaining amount will be secured through Croatian national sources.

World.title: Approval Granted for Construction of Key Croatian Four-Lane Road Section
World.content:
July the 28th, 2026 – Approval has been granted for the construction of a key Croatian four-lane road section, and it is being hailed as one of the country’s most significant motorway projects.

Croatian drivers are a step closer to improved transport links after the government approved the construction of one of the country’s most important road projects. The decision clears the way for the development of a new four-lane section that is expected to improve traffic flow, increase road safety and strengthen connections between key parts of the national road network.

The approval relates to the 21.9-kilometre Podravska Expressway section between Pitomača and Virovitica, after the Ministry of Environmental Protection and Green Transition completed the environmental impact assessment and declared the project environmentally acceptable.

The project has received official approval following the completion of the necessary planning procedures, allowing preparations for construction to move forward. Poslovni reports that the new road section will be built with four traffic lanes, significantly increasing capacity compared with the existing road and helping to reduce congestion, particularly during periods of heavy traffic. According to the project plans, the upgraded route will form part of a wider transport corridor designed to improve connections between regions, shorten travel times and support economic development. The investment is also expected to enhance access for businesses, tourism and freight transport.

The planned road will include modern infrastructure designed to meet current safety standards, with features aimed at improving traffic efficiency and reducing the risk of accidents. Officials say the project represents one of the country’s most significant transport investments in recent years.

The approval marks an important milestone, but several stages remain before construction begins, including the completion of procurement procedures and the selection of contractors. Once the boots are actually on the ground, the project is expected to be carried out in multiple phases.

The new four-lane road is otherwise a large part of Croatia’s broader strategy to modernise its transport infrastructure and improve connectivity across the country. Once completed, it is expected to make journeys faster, safer and more reliable for both local residents and visitors, while supporting long-term economic growth.

World.title: Estonian women's épée team narrowly miss world title, take silver
World.content:
Estonia's women's épée foursome took silver at the World Championships in Hong Kong after going down to Olympic champions Italy by just one point, in the final.

The last time the women's épée team reached the World Championship final was nearly a decade ago, in 2017. That time, the team defeated China to take gold.

After a disappointing run in the individual women's épée event late last week and over the weekend, the seventh-seeded women's épée foursome, consisting of Veronika Zuikova, reigning European champion Katrina Lehis, and two veterans from the 2017 final, Julia Beljajeva and Irina Embrich, went all the way to the final to narrowly lose 31–30 to the Italians.

Lehis was crowned European champion last month. Three of the four (Lehis, Beljajeva, and Embrich) were part of the team which took gold at the 2020 Tokyo Olympics (held in 2021), while Beljajeva and Embrich were in the 2017 final, which Estonia won. Lehis also took bronze at the individual event in Tokyo.

Progress to the final

The team first faced Romania in the round of 32. They claimed a 36–25 victory in that match.

Katrina Lehis Source: FIE - International Fencing Federation

Next up came Canada, which Estonia cruised past with a 45–25 victory; Estonia lost just one of the nine individual bouts in that round.

In the quarterfinals, Estonia took on reigning world champions and Paris Olympic silver medalists France, who had defeated Chinese Taipei 45–18 and Israel 45–39.

Estonia made a superb start as Beljajeva blanked Alexandra Louis Marie von Kerssenbrock 5–0, Embrich scored the first two touches of her bout to give Estonia a 9–2 lead, and Lehis then defeated Marie-Florence Candassamy 4–2. After Beljajeva's touch in the fifth bout, the Estonians had stretched their lead to 19–7, and their advantage remained at at least 10 touches throughout. Embrich's victory over Candassamy extended Estonia's lead to 30–17.

The French attacked aggressively in the final two bouts. Von Kerssenbrock edged Lehis 9–8, and France's fourth team member, Auriane Mallo-Breton, beat Beljajeva 8–7, but Estonia's lead held up and the team advanced to the semifinals with a 45–34 win.

In the semifinals, the Estonian women faced Hungary, European Championship silver medalists three times over the past four years. Hungary had beaten the U.S. 43–38 in their quarterfinal.

Lehis beat top fencer Blanka Nagy 7–4 in the second bout, while Beljajeva again excelled, defeating the youngest member of the Hungarian team 4–1 to give Estonia a 14–9 overall lead after the fourth bout.

Estonia's Veronika Zuikova , Katrina Lehis, Julia Beljajeva and Irina Embrich took silver in the FIE World Championships in Hong Kong . Source: FIE/Bizzi Team

Embrich briefly found herself in trouble against Nagy, 27 years her junior, but then scored three consecutive touches. After Beljajeva's 3–2 victory over Lili Buki, Lehis entered the final bout holding a three-touch lead against Hungary's top fencer, Eszter Muhari. Lehis withstood the attacks of the Paris Olympic bronze medalist, won the bout 15–12, and sent Estonia into the final with a 42–34 overall victory.

Italy, who took olympic gold in Paris two years ago, edged South Korea 45–44 in a thrilling semifinal to set up the showdown with Estonia.

The final

The final in Hong Kong started at 3 p.m. Estonian time Tuesday.

Alberta Santuccio defeated Beljajeva 2–0 in the opening bout, and Estonia spent the rest of the final chasing the deficit, which got as narrow as one point early on in the tournament as Beljajeva's victory in her second bout, when things were 11–10 in the Italians' favor. Lehis however then lost 4–0 down to Giulia Rizzi in the sixth bout, allowing the olympic champions to extend their lead to six touches. Embrich and Beljajeva together managed to pull Estonia one touch closer, leaving Lehis to begin the final bout trailing 24–19.

While Lehis expertly put her Italian opponent under pressure and gradually reduced Estonia's deficit – With 40 seconds remaining, Lehis closed to within a single touch, but there was simply too little time left. The final seconds featured five consecutive double touches, leaving Italy to claim a narrow 31–30 victory.

Editor's note: This piece was updated to include the final result.

World.title: Photos: Demolition begins at Tallinn's Eesti Näitused expo center
World.content:
Demolition has begun at Tallinn's former Eesti Näitused expo center, where a new residential development is planned along Pirita tee.

The last trade fair at the center was held in mid-June.

Mait Allas, CEO of real estate developer Metro Capital, told ERR that demolition of the Soviet-era exposition halls, which began Tuesday, is expected to take two to three months.

Metro Capital plans to begin construction of Marienberg Quarter on the nearly 7-hectare site in 2028, with plans including apartment buildings, a kindergarten, a pedestrian boulevard and green spaces.

Some nearby residents previously challenged the plans in court, but those disputes have since been resolved, and the developer says it hopes to reach agreements with neighbors going forward.

The project timeline now depends partly on approval of the site's zoning plan, which is nearing completion. Allas said he hopes it will be approved this fall, allowing design work to begin soon after.
